name: Aider
description: Aider is an open-source AI pair-programming tool that edits code from a terminal inside a Git repository. It connects to supported language-model providers and keeps the workflow reviewable through diffs, commits, tests, and linting.
priceDetails: The CLI is open source and free to install; model-provider API usage is billed separately according to the provider.
install: python -m pip install aider-install
gettingStarted: Install the official launcher with python -m pip install aider-install, or use the documented Windows PowerShell installer.
Change into a Git repository and run aider with a supported model and provider key, for example aider --model sonnet --api-key anthropic=<key>.
Add only the files relevant to the task, ask for one focused change, then inspect /diff before accepting it.
Configure repository-specific lint and test commands, and run them after each meaningful edit.
bestFor: Terminal-first pair programming in an existing Git repository
Multi-file refactors where every change should be reviewable
Coding loops that combine repository context with lint and test feedback
Teams that want a local CLI while choosing their own model provider
strengths: Repository-aware context and a live repo map help the model navigate code
Git integration supports diffs, commits, and undo-friendly iteration
Lint and test commands can be run as part of the edit loop
Provider/model selection is configurable with flags or environment variables
Open-source CLI can be installed on Windows, macOS, and Linux
usageNotes: Aider is local-first, but model requests and any selected provider API usage leave the machine; review provider retention and billing.
Keep API keys in environment variables or an .env file and never commit them.
Use /run only for commands you are comfortable executing locally; review shell commands and their output.
Automatic commits, linting, and tests depend on repository configuration; inspect the diff and test results before merging.
Model aliases, provider support, pricing, and context limits change; verify the current model list before selecting one.

name: Cursor
description: Cursor is an AI code editor and coding-agent workspace for understanding, planning, writing, reviewing, and refactoring software across local desktop projects and optional cloud agents.
bestFor: Multi-file implementation, refactoring, and debugging in an editor
Codebase exploration with search, rules, and agent tools
Teams that need reviewable local changes or isolated cloud tasks
Automated terminal or CI runs through the Cursor CLI
strengths: Agent mode can combine codebase context, edits, terminal tools, and a selected model
Ask, Agent, and custom modes let teams choose exploration versus execution
Project rules provide reusable instructions with conditional or always-on application
Cloud agents can work in isolated environments and return logs, screenshots, and pull-request changes
Privacy mode, sandboxing, hooks, and enterprise controls help govern agent access
gettingStarted: Install Cursor for your desktop OS, sign in, and open a repository.
Create project rules for conventions and safety constraints before delegating broad changes.
Use Ask for read-only exploration; switch to Agent for implementation and keep the first task narrowly scoped.
Review the diff, terminal output, and tests locally before merging or accepting a cloud-agent result.
For automation, install the Cursor CLI and store CURSOR_API_KEY as a secret rather than in the repository.
usageNotes: Agent permissions can include file edits, shell commands, network access, and MCP tools; choose approvals and sandbox mode deliberately.
Cloud/background agents run remotely with repository, dependency, secret, and network access configured for that run; grant only what the task requires.
Treat repository instructions and external content as untrusted input and review generated commands for prompt-injection or destructive behavior.
Privacy mode and retention controls vary by plan and organization; confirm current settings before using sensitive code.
Model availability, quotas, pricing, and CLI flags change; verify current Cursor documentation before pinning a workflow.
priceDetails: Cursor offers plan-based access with usage limits; cloud agents and model usage may consume additional included or metered quota. Check the live pricing page for current limits.

name: OpenRouter
description: OpenRouter is a unified, OpenAI-compatible gateway for hundreds of AI models. It exposes one API while letting you choose models, providers, fallbacks, routing rules, and data policies per request.
bestFor: Integrating multiple model vendors behind one API surface
Rapid model comparison by capability, price, context, and availability
Production routing with provider order, fallbacks, and parameter checks
Applications that need optional BYOK or zero-data-retention constraints
strengths: OpenAI SDK-compatible base URL reduces integration changes
Model catalog and metadata endpoints expose current capabilities and pricing
Provider preferences support ordered fallback, allowlists, and required-parameter checks
Multimodal, tool-use, reasoning, and structured-output parameters are normalized where supported
Routing and privacy controls can be configured per request or account
gettingStarted: Create an OpenRouter account and API key; add credits or confirm the selected free/BYOK path.
Send a small request to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 using an OpenAI-compatible client and a current model slug.
Query the live /api/v1/models catalog before choosing a model and record the exact slug in configuration.
Set provider order, fallbacks, and require_parameters only after testing the requested model features.
Add usage limits, retries, timeout handling, and spend monitoring before exposing the key to production traffic.
usageNotes: OpenRouter forwards prompts to third-party model providers; review each provider’s retention, training, residency, and safety policies.
Provider routing can change latency, output behavior, and data path; use explicit order/only constraints when reproducibility matters.
A model may accept a parameter but a selected provider may not; require_parameters can filter incompatible providers.
API keys belong on a server or secret manager, never in browser code or committed files.
Model availability, prices, rate limits, free quotas, and BYOK terms change; check the live catalog and pricing before budgeting.
priceDetails: OpenRouter usage is generally billed per selected model/provider token rates; free models, credits, rate limits, and BYOK behavior vary over time.
install: npm install @openrouter/sdk

name: Groq
description: A managed inference platform and OpenAI-compatible API focused on very low-latency execution of supported language, multimodal, and audio models.
bestFor: Low-latency chat and completion workloads
OpenAI-compatible migrations where fast inference matters
Streaming responses and function/tool calling in agents

Send a server-side request to https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions with Bearer authentication.
Choose a currently available model from the model catalog and provide messages.
Enable stream:true for incremental output or tools for function-calling workflows.
usageNotes: Keep GROQ_API_KEY in environment variables or a secret manager; never ship it to browsers.
The API is OpenAI-compatible but model names, context limits, tool support, and deprecations are Groq-specific.
Use usage and x_groq timing fields to measure latency and token consumption in production.
Rate limits and quotas depend on the account and model; inspect current Console limits before load testing.
Browser search and tool calls can introduce external-content and prompt-injection risks; validate tool arguments and outputs.
priceDetails: A free developer allowance and paid usage are available; current model pricing, quotas, and rate limits are listed in Groq Console.

Store the key as `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` in a server-side environment or secret manager.
Install the official Python or JavaScript SDK, or configure the OpenAI client with `base_url` / `baseURL` set to `https://api.cerebras.ai/v1`.
Send a first request to `POST https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/chat/completions` with a supported model and messages.
Use the Cloud Console playground to test models and prompts before integrating the API.

Use streaming for incremental output and configure reasoning parameters only for models that support them.
Rate limits depend on the account tier and current plan; implement exponential backoff for temporary rate-limit errors.
The Free Trial tier includes initial credits, while Developer and Enterprise tiers provide different limits and support; verify current pricing and quotas before promising costs.
For production workloads, use server-side key management, access controls, usage monitoring, and explicit rate limits.
priceDetails: Free tier with $5 credits; Developer tier pay-per-token from $0.35/M input tokens; Pro $50/month; Enterprise custom pricing

name: Windsurf
description: An agentic AI-powered IDE developed by Codeium, featuring the Cascade AI assistant for deep codebase context awareness, multi-file editing, and task execution .
bestFor: Developers who want an AI-first desktop IDE with an agent that can understand and modify an entire codebase.
Multi-file implementation, refactoring, debugging, and other multi-step coding tasks.
Teams that want planning, terminal execution, web and documentation search, MCP integrations, workflows, and app deployment in one IDE.
Developers who prefer a visual editor with real-time codebase awareness and model selection instead of a terminal-only workflow.
strengths: Cascade is the built-in agentic assistant with codebase search, tool calling, terminal access, checkpoints, real-time awareness, and linter integration.
Cascade supports dedicated Code, Plan, and Ask modes: Code can make changes, Plan prepares an implementation plan, and Ask is read-only.
Selected editor or terminal text can be included automatically when opening Cascade with `Cmd/Ctrl+L`.
Integrated features include web and documentation search through `@web` and `@docs`, Memories and Rules, MCP servers, Workflows, and App Deploys.
Long-running tasks can use an internal plan and a conversation todo list; plan files can be continued across sessions from `~/.windsurf/plans`.
The editor supports selecting an AI model from the Cascade conversation interface.
gettingStarted: Download and install Windsurf from the official website for your operating system.
Launch Windsurf, sign in if prompted, and open an existing project or create a new one.
Open Cascade with `Cmd/Ctrl+L`, then start with Ask mode for read-only exploration of the codebase.
Use Plan mode for a complex feature so Cascade can inspect the repository and write an implementation plan before editing.
Switch to Code mode or use the plan file's Implement action when you are ready to apply changes.
Review the proposed diff, run the project's tests and linter, and use checkpoints to recover safely when experimenting.
usageNotes: Code mode can create, edit, and delete files, run terminal commands, search and analyze the project, install dependencies, and execute multi-step tasks autonomously.
Ask mode is read-only: Cascade can search and analyze the codebase but cannot make changes.
Plan mode writes a detailed implementation plan to an external Markdown file; plans can be refined and resumed in later sessions.
Treat terminal commands, dependency installation, MCP servers, web access, and app deployment as privileged capabilities; review commands and permissions before approving them.
Use project rules and memories to make recurring conventions explicit, but keep sensitive values such as API keys and credentials out of prompts, rules, and repository files.
Web and documentation search adds external context; verify generated code and citations against the original source before relying on them.
Model availability and feature access can vary by plan and may change, so confirm current limits in the Windsurf account and documentation.
priceDetails: Free, Pro (estimated $20/mo), Teams ($40/seat/mo), Max ($200/mo)

name: GitHub Copilot
description: An AI-powered coding assistant developed by GitHub that provides code completions and chat-based support to help developers write code faster and more efficiently .
bestFor: Developers who want code completion, chat, and agentic help inside supported IDEs and GitHub workflows.
Teams that need GitHub-native pull request review, issue-to-pull-request automation, and human review gates.
Terminal-based coding tasks with explicit file and command permissions via GitHub Copilot CLI.

An official SDK communicates with Copilot CLI through JSON-RPC and supports custom agents, MCP integrations, hooks, session management, and app integrations.
gettingStarted: Choose Copilot Free or a paid Copilot plan, then install the GitHub Copilot extension in a supported IDE and sign in to GitHub.
For terminal use, install Node.js 22 or later, then run `npm install -g @github/copilot` and authenticate with `copilot login`.
Use browser, device-code, or token-based login; the CLI stores the resulting token in the system credential store or its configuration.
If Copilot is organization-provided, an administrator must enable the applicable Copilot CLI policy before CLI access works.
usageNotes: Review every agent change, command, and pull request before merging; GitHub frames agentic features around human oversight and review.

Premium requests are allowance-based. After the monthly allowance is exhausted, included models may still be available, but may have variable latency and rate limits; users can upgrade or set a budget where supported.
Use the personal policy for suggestions matching public code: block mode withholds matches or near-matches; allowed matches can be inspected with source and license details where supported.
Do not expose GitHub tokens. CLI login credentials are sensitive even when stored by the credential manager.
For GitHub Actions using the Copilot SDK, grant only the documented minimum workflow permissions needed, such as `contents: read` and `copilot-requests: write`.
priceDetails: Free plan available; paid plans start at approximately $10/month

bestFor: Checking whether later literature supports or challenges a paper or claim
Searching full-text articles and citation statements beyond titles and abstracts
Auditing manuscript references for retractions, notices, and contrasting evidence
Grounding AI research assistants with peer-reviewed literature and citation context
strengths: Smart Citations pair citation tallies with the classified statements behind them
Search can query full text and citation statements with filters
Reference Check flags retractions, editorial notices, and contrasting evidence
Assistant answers are linked back to the literature it used
API and MCP surfaces support agent and enterprise integrations
gettingStarted: Open scite.ai and search for a paper, DOI, claim, or topic.
Inspect the Smart Citation classification and read the underlying citation context.
Use Reference Check for a manuscript bibliography and review every warning manually.
For integrations, request API access or connect the official MCP endpoint with approved credentials.
usageNotes: A supporting/contrasting label is evidence about citation context, not a definitive verdict on scientific truth.
Coverage, full-text access, publisher licensing, and classification quality vary by discipline and source.
Use the API/MCP only with least-privilege keys and avoid sending confidential manuscripts unless your agreement allows it.
Keep a human researcher in the loop for inclusion decisions, systematic reviews, and clinical or policy conclusions.
Subscription, API, data-feed, and institutional terms change; verify current pricing and entitlements in the live account.
priceDetails: Scite offers web access, institutional plans, and separate API/data products; current pricing and limits should be confirmed with Scite.

name: NotebookLM
description: Google’s source-grounded notebook assistant for asking questions about curated documents, websites, videos, and other sources, then generating summaries and Studio artifacts such as audio or video overviews.
bestFor: Understanding a private set of project or study sources
Building briefings, FAQs, timelines, and study guides from documents
Generating Audio Overviews and other artifacts from notebook material
Collaborative knowledge bases that need source-scoped chat
strengths: Notebook chat answers are grounded in the notebook’s selected sources
Supports PDFs, websites, YouTube, audio, copied text, and Google content depending on surface
Studio can generate Audio Overviews, Video Overviews, infographics, slide decks, notes, and mind maps
Notebook changes and custom instructions can sync with Gemini notebooks
Mobile app supports source capture and offline audio downloads with feature limits
gettingStarted: Open NotebookLM and sign in with a supported Google account.
Create a notebook, add only the sources relevant to the question, and wait for indexing.
Ask focused questions and inspect the source citations before relying on an answer.
Use Studio for an artifact, then review the generated text/audio/video for omissions and errors before sharing.
usageNotes: NotebookLM chat is source-grounded, but Gemini chats may also use web search and other tools; confirm which surface you are using.
Shared notebooks and Gemini chat context have different visibility rules; private notebooks with Gemini chats may not be shareable.
Google states uploaded files and NotebookLM chats are not used to train foundational models unless you provide feedback, but review the current privacy terms.
AI responses and artifacts can contain errors; use primary sources and human review for education, research, or high-stakes decisions.
Feature availability, source limits, mobile parity, regional access, and paid-tier quotas change; verify current Help Center guidance.
priceDetails: NotebookLM has free and tiered Google account offerings; current limits, enterprise access, and paid features should be checked in Google’s live Help Center.

name: SciSpace
description: An AI research workspace for discovering and understanding scientific literature, with semantic paper search, Chat with PDF, Copilot explanations, literature-review workflows, writing tools, and citation support.
bestFor: Reading difficult papers with explanations for text, math, tables, and jargon
Searching beyond keyword matches with semantic relevance and citation trails
Chatting with uploaded PDFs and receiving location-linked answers
Drafting literature reviews, extracting data, and preparing research artifacts
strengths: Chat with PDF links answers to supporting locations in the source
Semantic search surfaces related research beyond exact keyword matches
SciSpace Agent supports multi-step literature search, screening, extraction, and drafting
Browser extension can explain highlighted text while reading a paper or report
Platform includes search, literature review, citation, writing, and presentation tools
gettingStarted: Open scispace.com and sign in or create an account.
Search for a topic or upload a PDF, then ask a focused question about the source.
Inspect the cited passage or source location before accepting an explanation.
For larger reviews, define scope and extraction fields, review the Agent’s output, and export only after human checking.
usageNotes: AI explanations and extracted fields can be wrong; verify against the full paper, tables, figures, and supplementary material.
Use semantic search and citation trails to discover candidates, but preserve a documented search protocol for systematic reviews.
Uploaded PDFs may contain unpublished or sensitive material; review current privacy, encryption, and retention terms before upload.
Browser-extension and account features may have different limits from the web app or Agent workflows.
Free quotas, premium features, language support, and Agent credits change; verify current plan details in SciSpace.
priceDetails: SciSpace offers free access with usage limits and paid tiers for higher quotas and advanced Agent/review features; verify current pricing live.

name: ResearchRabbit
description: A citation-network literature discovery platform that helps researchers search from seed papers, explore related work and authors, visualize connections, and organize findings into collections and projects.
bestFor: Finding related papers beyond keyword search
Citation chasing and visual mapping for literature reviews
Organizing reading lists, collections, notes, and collaborators
Exploring how papers and authors connect over time
strengths: Recommendations use citation and authorship relationships
Iterative rabbit-hole exploration refines discovery as seed papers are added
Interactive network and timeline views reveal research clusters and trends
Collections and Reading Lists keep candidate papers organized
Free tier includes core search, collections, uploads, and collaboration features
gettingStarted: Create a ResearchRabbit account and start a project or collection.
Add a few high-quality seed papers by title, DOI, or imported library.
Explore similar work, references, citations, and authors, then save relevant papers to collections.
Export or share the curated collection and verify coverage against your review protocol.
usageNotes: ResearchRabbit is a discovery and organization aid, not a complete systematic-review database; supplement it with protocol-driven database searches.
Recommendations depend on indexed metadata and citation links, so coverage can vary by field, venue, and publication type.
Use Signals and citation context as triage clues, then read the paper before judging quality or evidence.
Shared collections and library uploads can expose your research plans; review collaborators and access settings.
Free/RR+ features, seed limits, advanced search, and pricing change; verify current plan details.
priceDetails: ResearchRabbit offers a free core tier and an optional RR+ plan; current feature and project limits should be checked on the pricing page.

name: Connected Papers
description: A visual literature-discovery tool that builds an interactive graph of papers related to an origin paper using co-citation and bibliographic-coupling signals from the Semantic Scholar corpus.
bestFor: Exploring a research field from one or more strong seed papers
Finding foundational Prior Works and newer Derivative Works
Seeing clusters, influential papers, and topic evolution visually
Creating a reading path before running a formal systematic search
strengths: Graph nodes show relationships and similarity rather than a simple citation tree
Prior Works surfaces commonly cited foundational literature
Derivative Works highlights newer papers and reviews connected to the graph
List, graph, and timeline-style exploration support different review phases
Official API and Python client are available for programmatic graph access
gettingStarted: Open connectedpapers.com and enter a relevant paper title, DOI, or supported identifier.
Confirm the matched origin paper and generate its graph.
Inspect similar papers, Prior Works, Derivative Works, and author connections.
Save or export candidate references, then deduplicate and verify coverage in your formal review workflow.
usageNotes: Graphs are discovery aids built from citation relationships; absence from a graph does not mean a paper is irrelevant.
The underlying corpus and publisher coverage can vary by field, language, and publication type.
Use multiple seeds and a documented search protocol for systematic reviews instead of relying on one graph.
The official Python client requires an API key and Semantic Scholar paper IDs; keep credentials server-side.
Free graph limits, API access, exports, and subscription terms change; verify current pricing and quotas.
priceDetails: Connected Papers offers free and paid access with graph and API limits that may vary by account; verify current terms live.

name: Semantic Scholar
description: A scholarly search and data platform from AI2 with semantic paper discovery, paper/author metadata, citation and reference graphs, recommendations, and public Academic Graph and Datasets APIs.
bestFor: Relevance-ranked discovery when terminology varies
Retrieving paper metadata by DOI, arXiv, PMID, URL, or Semantic Scholar ID
Traversing citations and references for literature mapping
Programmatic academic search and dataset workflows
strengths: Paper search supports year, open-access PDF, and field-of-study filters
Paper detail endpoints accept multiple identifier formats and selectable fields
References and citation-related endpoints are paginated
Bulk search can return up to 1,000 records per call with continuation tokens
API key access uses the x-api-key header and raises throughput limits
gettingStarted: Search the web interface for a topic, paper, or author, or request an API key for programmatic work.
Call GET /graph/v1/paper/search with a query and only the fields your application needs.
Use a returned paperId, DOI, arXiv ID, or other supported identifier to fetch details and references.
Respect pagination, cache stable metadata, and review current API terms before large-scale harvesting.
usageNotes: paperId and corpusId are distinct identifiers; do not interchange them in API or dataset pipelines.
Public unauthenticated requests have lower rate limits; include x-api-key when approved and keep it server-side.
Bulk search is optimized for volume, not relevance, and nested citations/references are unavailable there.
Metadata and citation links support discovery but do not establish paper quality or scientific validity.
Rate limits, dataset access, coverage, and API policies change; verify current documentation and usage guidelines.
priceDetails: The web interface and public APIs are free to use within current rate limits and terms; verify high-volume dataset access separately.

name: Phind
description: A developer-focused AI answer and search experience for programming questions, technical research, debugging, and code explanations. Product availability and feature scope should be confirmed before relying on it.
bestFor: Exploring coding questions and error messages with conversational follow-up
Getting source-aware explanations and implementation ideas
Working with codebase context through the VS Code extension
Comparing technical approaches before checking primary documentation
strengths: Developer-first answer and search workflow
Source-backed responses are designed to keep research close to references
VS Code extension can use selected files and codebase context
Extension supports web search mentions and inline code assistance
Conversation history can be managed through account privacy settings
gettingStarted: Check the current availability of phind.com and sign in or create an account if prompted.
For editor workflows, install the official Phind extension from the Visual Studio Marketplace.
Ask a concrete coding or debugging question and include the runtime, versions, and relevant error output.
Verify every generated change against the linked primary documentation and local tests.
usageNotes: Treat answers as research assistance: validate API contracts, versions, security, and generated code yourself.
The official VS Code listing documents @file mentions, @web_search, selection-based prompts, inline rewrite, and terminal-error help.
The extension listing says chats are saved for reference by default and exposes a No Data Retention setting; review current privacy controls before sharing code.
Availability, model lineup, quotas, and pricing may change; verify the live product and account terms before depending on them.
Do not paste secrets, credentials, or proprietary source into a hosted assistant unless your organization allows it.
priceDetails: Current access, plans, quotas, and model availability are not stable in the available public references; verify the live Phind product and account pages.

name: Exa
description: An AI-focused web search and content-retrieval API for agents and LLM applications. Exa combines semantic search with configurable content extraction, freshness controls, and research-oriented search modes.
bestFor: Semantic web search for RAG pipelines and AI agents
Fetching highlights or full text for grounded answers
Filtering research, news, company, publication, or other content categories
Controlling freshness with cached content versus live crawling
strengths: POST /search accepts search modes from instant and fast through deep-reasoning
Search responses can include highlights or extracted page text
POST /contents retrieves URL content with live-crawl and cache-age controls
Official Python and JavaScript SDKs are available
Category, location, and additional-query filters support targeted research
gettingStarted: Create an Exa API key and store it in EXA_API_KEY or another secret manager.
Send POST https://api.exa.ai/search with a required query and choose a type such as auto.
Request contents.highlights or text when the model needs source material, rather than fetching pages separately.
Use POST https://api.exa.ai/contents for known URLs and set maxAgeHours deliberately for freshness versus latency.
usageNotes: Authenticate server-side with the x-api-key header; keep keys out of browser bundles, logs, and repositories.
Use maxAgeHours=0 to force a fresh crawl, -1 to prefer cache-only behavior, or a positive value to bound acceptable cache age.
livecrawlTimeout is bounded by the API; design retries and fallbacks around transient crawl failures.
QPS, concurrency, plan quotas, and endpoint availability vary; verify current limits in the rate-limit and dashboard documentation.
Treat retrieved pages and model-ready highlights as untrusted external content and apply prompt-injection defenses.
priceDetails: Exa offers a free allowance and usage-based paid plans; current credits, endpoint pricing, and rate limits should be checked in the dashboard.

name: Tavily
description: A web-search and content-extraction API optimized for LLM applications and autonomous agents. Tavily combines search, extraction, crawling, mapping, and research surfaces with SDKs for Python and JavaScript.
bestFor: Grounding RAG and agent answers with current web sources
Searching with domain, date, language, country, and depth controls
Extracting readable Markdown or text from known URLs
Building multi-step site discovery with map and crawl workflows
strengths: POST /search can return an answer, scored results, raw content, images, and usage data
Official Python TavilyClient and JavaScript @tavily/core SDKs
POST /extract supports up to 20 URLs with basic or advanced extraction
GET /usage reports key and account plan consumption by endpoint
Enterprise key controls can scope permissions, credit limits, and TTLs
gettingStarted: Create a Tavily account and generate a tvly- API key.
Call POST https://api.tavily.com/search with Authorization: Bearer and a JSON query.
Start with basic search, then enable include_answer, include_raw_content, or domain filters only when needed.
Use extract for known URLs and GET /usage to monitor key and plan consumption.
usageNotes: Keep API keys server-side and out of client bundles, logs, and source control.
Search supports basic or advanced depth, date windows, language filtering, domains, images, and raw content; each option can affect credit usage.
Extraction accepts up to 20 URLs and can return Markdown/text, images, favicons, and reranked chunks.
Keyless access is rate-limited; use authenticated keys for reliable integrations.
Credits, quotas, retention, and plan pricing change; verify current account terms and usage limits before production rollout.
priceDetails: Tavily offers free credits and paid usage plans; current credit rates, quotas, and plan details should be verified in the live dashboard.
install: pip install tavily-python

name: Brave Search API
description: A privacy-focused REST API backed by Brave's independent search index. It exposes structured web search and specialized verticals for applications that need current, source-grounded information.
bestFor: Adding current web results to chatbots, agents, and RAG pipelines
Building privacy-focused search, research, and monitoring experiences
Searching dedicated news, image, and video verticals from one API
Returning machine-readable results without scraping search pages
strengths: Independent index and privacy-first positioning
Simple REST interface with JSON responses
Dedicated web and news search documentation, plus additional verticals
Optional rich-result callbacks for supported vertical data
Pagination metadata helps clients request another page only when available
gettingStarted: Create an account in the Brave Search API dashboard.
Create or select a subscription and copy the generated subscription token.
Send a GET request to https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search with a required q parameter.
Pass the token in the X-Subscription-Token header, then parse the JSON response and its result sections.
usageNotes: Authentication uses the X-Subscription-Token request header; never expose the token in browser code or public repositories.
The web-search endpoint is GET /res/v1/web/search and requires q; the API also documents news and other vertical endpoints.
Check query.more_results_available before fetching another page to avoid unnecessary calls.
Set enable_rich_callback=1 when you need supported rich-data hints and callback keys.
Confirm current plan pricing, quotas, and rate limits in the dashboard before shipping production traffic.
priceDetails: Plan availability, quotas, and pricing are managed in the Brave Search API dashboard; verify current terms before launch.

name: YYLO
description: An open-source Node.js CLI orchestrator for governed coding-agent work. YYLO turns a task into an isolated worktree, runs validation and review through typed lifecycle stages, and produces receipt-backed merge and release-readiness evidence.
bestFor: Teams coordinating Pi, Codex, or other coding agents under one lifecycle
Repository changes that require a frozen target SHA and isolated worktree
Risk-based review queues with bounded repair and delta-review passes
Operators who need auditable task, validation, merge, and release gates
strengths: Typed task state protects the target commit and task boundaries
Dedicated branches/worktrees isolate agent changes from the controller
Risk-based merge queue limits reviewer passes and terminates deterministically
No-model canary and watch commands help verify the runner before agent use
Skills are versioned and installed separately from the CLI
gettingStarted: Install Node.js 20.10+, npm, and Git, then install `@yylo/cli` globally.
Run `yy --version` and initialize a small task with an explicitly selected subagent.
Start work with `yy task start TASK_ID`, inspect the generated worktree, and run the no-model canary.
Let the merge queue validate and review the frozen candidate before accepting any branch or release output.
usageNotes: YYLO orchestrates agents; model credentials, provider limits, and agent safety remain external concerns.
Treat the protected target SHA, controller metadata, and task worktree as separate authorities and do not edit them interchangeably.
The bounded review queue is intentional: investigate findings after the terminal state instead of expecting infinite auto-repair.
Keep skills and task definitions versioned, reviewed, and free of credentials or destructive defaults.
CLI behavior, supported subagents, Node requirements, and skills packages can change; verify the current README before automation.
priceDetails: YYLO is open-source; costs come from the coding agents, model providers, CI runners, and repository hosting it orchestrates.
install: npm install --global '@yylo/cli@latest'
start: yy

commands.label: Initialize a task workspace
commands.command: yy init --task "Document the onboarding path" --subagent pi

name: ChatGPT
description: ChatGPT is OpenAI’s hosted assistant and workspace for conversation, writing, analysis, coding, research, files, images, voice, and—when available—agentic tasks. ChatGPT subscriptions and the OpenAI API are separate products with separate access and billing.
bestFor: Iterative drafting, analysis, research, and coding in one workspace
Working from uploaded PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, images, and other files
Long-running projects that need chats, files, instructions, and project memory
Voice, web search, data analysis, Canvas, and other interactive workflows
strengths: Projects group chats, files, and custom instructions with built-in project memory
Data Analysis can run code to inspect and visualize supported structured files
Canvas supports co-writing, editing, and code-focused iteration
Web search, image generation, voice, and file tools are available according to plan and workspace settings
ChatGPT Work/Codex and agent features can extend workflows when the account permits them
gettingStarted: Create or sign in to a ChatGPT account at chatgpt.com.
Start a chat with a concrete goal; attach source files or images only when they add necessary context.
For ongoing work, create a Project, add custom instructions and reference files, and choose the appropriate memory setting.
Use web search or Data Analysis when freshness or computation matters, then inspect citations, generated files, and intermediate results.
Before sharing sensitive material, review account/workspace data controls, retention, connected apps, and plan limits.
usageNotes: ChatGPT consumer, team, enterprise, and education plans have different models, tools, quotas, and admin controls; availability also varies by region and workspace.
Projects retain chats and files as context; project-only memory and default memory have different boundaries.
Uploaded files, prompts, generated content, and connected apps may contain sensitive data; check retention and training settings before use.
Agent, Work, Codex, web search, voice, and data-analysis actions can have separate limits and may require confirmation for external effects.
ChatGPT responses can be incorrect or incomplete; verify important legal, medical, financial, security, and production decisions.
priceDetails: ChatGPT has Free and paid personal/workspace plans with plan-specific limits; the OpenAI API is a separate, usage-billed product.

name: Claude
description: Anthropic’s Claude product and API family for writing, analysis, coding, document work, and agentic applications. Claude.ai is the hosted assistant; the Messages API is the developer surface.
bestFor: Long-form writing, analysis, and coding with project context
Document conversations and interactive Artifacts
Tool-using backends with streaming and structured outputs
Applications needing prompt caching, vision, or extended reasoning on supported models
strengths: Claude.ai Projects organize reusable instructions and reference material
Artifacts provide a dedicated editable output surface
Messages API supports tools, streaming, prompt caching, and structured outputs
SDKs are available for multiple server-side languages
Hosted and API surfaces can be evaluated separately for privacy, limits, and billing
gettingStarted: Create or sign in to Claude.ai for the hosted workspace, or create an Anthropic Console key for API use.
Use Projects for persistent instructions and source files; use a normal chat for a one-off question.
For API work, install an official SDK, set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY server-side, and send a small Messages API request.
Add tools or streaming incrementally, then test token limits, tool approvals, and error handling.
usageNotes: Claude.ai and the Anthropic API are separate products with different plans, retention, quotas, and authentication.
Tool-use functions can execute external actions; validate arguments and require approval for writes, shell commands, or sensitive operations.
Uploaded files, project knowledge, prompts, and API logs may contain sensitive data; review current privacy and retention controls.
Model names, context windows, regional availability, and feature access change; verify the current model documentation before pinning.
Citations and generated content need human review, especially for legal, medical, financial, or security decisions.
priceDetails: Claude.ai plans and Anthropic API usage are billed separately; current consumer, team, enterprise, and model rates should be checked in the live account.

name: Gemini
description: Google Gemini is Google’s cloud assistant for text, images, files, voice, and web-connected tasks. The Gemini consumer app is separate from the Gemini API/Google AI Studio and Vertex AI developer products, which have different keys, quotas, models, and billing.
bestFor: Everyday conversational work in a Google-account-based workspace
Multimodal questions over text, images, and supported uploaded files
Voice and mobile workflows where regional availability is confirmed
Prototyping Gemini API applications through Google AI Studio or Vertex AI
strengths: Web and mobile apps support multimodal conversations and follow-up context
Google account integration can connect Gemini to supported Google ecosystem features
Gemini API offers official SDKs, streaming, multimodal input, and function calling
Developer access can target the Gemini Developer API or Vertex AI with separate configuration
Availability, languages, plans, and age/region eligibility are documented explicitly
gettingStarted: Sign in with an eligible Google account and open gemini.google.com, or install the supported mobile app.
Start with a focused prompt; attach an image or file only when the task needs it and review generated answers.
For development, create a key in Google AI Studio or configure a Vertex AI project, then use the official Google GenAI SDK.
Choose a current model from the live developer catalog and test text, multimodal, streaming, or tool calls separately.
Before production use, set quotas, safety settings, logging, data controls, and regional availability for the target users.
usageNotes: Gemini consumer features and the Gemini API are separate products; do not assume an app subscription grants API quota or vice versa.
Web/mobile app availability, languages, plan features, age requirements, and connected-app access vary by region and account.
Uploaded content and conversations may be retained or processed under account/workspace settings; review Google privacy and activity controls.
Function calling and external tools execute in your application, not automatically inside the model; validate arguments and require approval for side effects.
Model names, context limits, pricing, quotas, safety behavior, and API revisions change; verify current Google documentation before pinning.
priceDetails: The Gemini app has free and paid Google AI plans with feature-specific limits; Gemini Developer API and Vertex AI usage are billed separately.

name: Grok
description: Grok is xAI’s conversational assistant for text, reasoning, coding, multimodal input, and current information. The hosted Grok app and xAI API are separate surfaces: the app can search public X/web context, while the API exposes Grok models, tools, files, and streaming for developers.
bestFor: Current-event questions that benefit from web or public X search
Conversational brainstorming, writing, reasoning, and coding
Multimodal or file-based analysis in the hosted app or API
Developer integrations using an OpenAI-compatible xAI endpoint
strengths: Hosted Grok can combine conversation with public X and web search where enabled
xAI API supports OpenAI SDK compatibility at https://api.x.ai/v1
Responses and chat APIs support streaming, files, and tool calls such as web/X search and code execution
Official SDKs are available for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript workflows
X privacy controls cover training use, personalization, and conversation-history management
gettingStarted: Open Grok on grok.com or in the supported X web/mobile experience and sign in.
Ask a focused question; request web/X search when freshness matters and inspect the cited sources.
For development, create an xAI API key, keep XAI_API_KEY server-side, and select a current Grok model.
Use the official SDK or OpenAI SDK with baseURL https://api.x.ai/v1, then test a small response before enabling tools or files.
Add timeouts, spend limits, tool-approval checks, and logging redaction before production use.
usageNotes: The consumer app and xAI API have different accounts, limits, features, retention, and billing; do not assume one grants access to the other.
Search results and public X posts can be incomplete, manipulated, or unavailable; verify consequential claims independently.
Tool calls and code execution can create external side effects; validate arguments and require approval for writes, network actions, or sensitive operations.
Prompts, uploaded files, outputs, and X interactions may be processed under separate privacy controls; review current settings and retention terms.
Model IDs, context windows, pricing, rate limits, regional access, and API behavior change; check current xAI docs before pinning.
priceDetails: Grok app access follows current X/xAI plan availability; xAI API usage is billed by model and token/tool usage with separate quotas and terms.

name: DeepSeek
description: DeepSeek provides a hosted chat assistant and a separate developer API for reasoning, coding, and general-purpose models. The API uses an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions interface with streaming, JSON output, reasoning controls, and function calling.
bestFor: Reasoning and coding conversations in the hosted DeepSeek app
Applications that need an OpenAI-compatible DeepSeek endpoint
Structured JSON generation and function/tool calling
Testing reasoning effort and streaming behavior with current models
strengths: Consumer chat and developer API are documented as separate products
API uses https://api.deepseek.com with familiar OpenAI SDK request shapes
Thinking/reasoning controls expose deliberate effort settings for supported models
JSON mode, streaming, and function tools support structured application workflows
Official docs publish current model, endpoint, and pricing details
gettingStarted: Open DeepSeek Chat and create an account for interactive use, or create a developer-platform account for API access.
For API work, create DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in a secret manager and configure an OpenAI client with base_url=https://api.deepseek.com.
Select a current model from the live documentation, send a small non-streaming request, then test streaming or reasoning mode.
Use response_format json_object only with a prompt that clearly requests JSON, and validate the parsed schema.
If enabling function calling, allowlist functions, validate arguments, and require approval before external side effects.
usageNotes: The chat site and API have separate authentication, quotas, privacy terms, and billing; an app account is not an API integration.
Reasoning output, token limits, model context, and supported parameters vary by model; confirm the current API reference.
Keep API keys server-side and redact prompts, tool arguments, and outputs from logs when they contain sensitive data.
Tool calling can invoke application code but does not make that code safe; validate input and enforce authorization independently.
DeepSeek responses can be incorrect or incomplete; verify consequential facts and protect against prompt injection in retrieved content.
priceDetails: DeepSeek Chat availability and developer API pricing are separate; API usage is billed by model/token and current quotas and rates may change.

name: Kimi
description: Kimi is Moonshot AI’s hosted assistant for chat, long-context document work, multimodal input, research, and agent-style tasks. The Kimi app is separate from the Moonshot API, which offers OpenAI-compatible endpoints for developers.
bestFor: Reading, extracting, and synthesizing long documents
Bilingual Chinese/English writing, research, and follow-up conversations
Multimodal questions over supported images and files
Developer integrations that need an OpenAI-compatible Moonshot endpoint
strengths: Long-context models are designed for large document and multi-step tasks
Hosted app supports web/mobile conversations and workspace-style workflows
Moonshot API accepts OpenAI SDK requests at https://api.moonshot.ai/v1
API supports multimodal messages, file extraction, streaming, and function tools
Official docs distinguish consumer availability from developer authentication and billing
gettingStarted: Create or sign in to Kimi at kimi.com and start a focused chat or supported task workflow.
Attach only the documents or images needed, ask for citations or extracted evidence, and compare the answer with the source.
For API use, create a Moonshot API key, store MOONSHOT_API_KEY server-side, and configure an OpenAI-compatible client with the documented base URL.
Test a small chat request before adding file extraction, multimodal input, streaming, or search/crawl tools.
Set token, timeout, retry, and spend limits before exposing the API to production traffic.
usageNotes: The Kimi app and Moonshot API have separate accounts, plans, limits, retention, and billing; do not conflate app access with API quota.
Long context does not guarantee perfect retrieval; inspect chunking, file extraction, citations, and omitted details.
Uploaded files and prompts may contain sensitive data; review Moonshot retention, training, regional processing, and deletion controls.
Function tools such as search or crawl execute in your application; validate URLs and arguments and require approval for side effects.
Model IDs, context windows, supported file types, region availability, pricing, and API behavior change; verify current docs before pinning.
priceDetails: Kimi app plans and Moonshot API usage are separate; API calls are billed according to current model/token rates and quotas.

name: Qwen Chat
description: Qwen Chat is Alibaba’s hosted interface for the Qwen family, with conversational, reasoning, coding, multimodal, and agent-style experiences where available. It is separate from Qwen open-weight downloads and Alibaba Cloud/DashScope developer APIs.
bestFor: Trying Qwen chat, reasoning, coding, and multimodal modes without local setup
Long-context and multilingual conversations in a hosted workspace
Comparing Qwen capabilities before selecting a local runtime or API provider
Everyday document, image, and agent-style tasks supported by the current product
strengths: One hosted product surface exposes multiple Qwen model experiences
Qwen models support multilingual text and, in supported variants, vision/audio and tool use
Open-weight Qwen checkpoints can be downloaded for local inference and fine-tuning
DashScope and other providers offer separate developer APIs for production integration
Product and model availability can be checked independently from local deployment choices
gettingStarted: Open chat.qwen.ai and sign in if the selected feature requires an account.

Browser research, pagination and workflow automation with typed outputs
Teams already using Playwright that want AI-assisted page understanding

Launch Playwright, wrap a page with agentql.wrap_async(), and navigate to a test URL

Call page.query_data(query), validate the returned schema, and add pagination only when needed

API keys belong in environment variables, never notebooks committed to Git

pip install agentql
playwright install chromium

import agentql
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async with async_playwright() as p:
    browser = await p.chromium.launch()
    page = await agentql.wrap_async(await browser.new_page())
    await page.goto("https://example.com")
    data = await page.query_data("{ title }")
