Natural-language prompts guide the kind of detail or transformation added during enhancement.
Creativity, HDR, and Resemblance controls balance new detail, contrast, and fidelity to the source.
Workflows cover portraits, illustrations, landscapes, films, graphic design, games, architecture, food, and 3D renders.
Magnific is available as a standalone web tool and is also surfaced in Freepik/Magnific plans, with API access for image/video enhancement and related operations.
Paid plans and API workflows are credit-based; API dashboards can create keys, monitor usage, and set spend limits.
gettingStarted: Open https://magnific.ai/ or the current Magnific/Freepik AI suite and sign in.
Upload an image, choose an upscale/enhance workflow, and describe the desired detail, material, style, or restoration constraints.
Start with conservative Creativity/HDR/Resemblance values, compare the output with the original, and iterate only where artifacts are acceptable.
Use the result for downstream editing or export after checking facial identity, text, edges, textures, and color fidelity.
For API automation, create an API key, preload credit balance, set spend limits, and call the documented upscaler/image endpoints from a secured server.
usageNotes: Generative enhancement can hallucinate details and alter identity, text, logos, product geometry, or texture; it is not a pixel-perfect restoration guarantee.
Subscription pricing and feature availability change; current Magnific/Freepik plans use credits with higher tiers adding more models, private workflows, API, and commercial licensing.
API usage is billed separately or through the current credit system depending on account setup; inspect the live API pricing before production.
Review commercial, stock, likeness, and copyright terms for the source and output. Paid plans may provide commercial rights, but third-party assets keep their own restrictions.
Cloud GPU processing is required and refunds may be limited by the service terms; test a representative image before buying a large plan.
Do not upload confidential or regulated images without approval, and never expose API keys in client-side code.
priceDetails: Paid, credit-based service. Standalone and current Freepik/Magnific plans differ by product; higher tiers provide more credits, private generation, advanced models, API access, and commercial licensing. Verify live pricing before purchase.
install: Open https://magnific.ai/ or use Magnific tools inside the current Freepik AI suite; no local runtime is required.
start: Upload an image, set upscale/enhancement prompt and creativity controls, run the job, compare with the source, then download or pass it to your design workflow.

name: Civitai
description: Community model hub and creator platform for discovering, downloading, sharing, and using Stable Diffusion and other generative media models, LoRAs, embeddings, and workflows.
bestFor: Finding checkpoints, LoRAs, textual inversions, VAEs, and model versions for image-generation pipelines.
Comparing creator samples, prompts, metadata, base models, hashes, ratings, and usage licenses before downloading.
Sharing models and generated images with community feedback, collections, creator profiles, and optional monetization.
Developers indexing model metadata, versions, hashes, files, and download URLs through Civitai’s public REST API.
strengths: Model pages expose versions, base-model information, trained words, sample images, generation metadata, ratings, creator details, and downloadable files.
The hub supports a broad ecosystem of checkpoints, LoRAs, embeddings, textual inversions, and community workflows for local or hosted Stable Diffusion tooling.
Public REST endpoints cover model discovery, model versions, hashes, creators, images, and downloads; API docs are maintained in the official developer repository.
Users can share generations, prompts, resources, comments, ratings, collections, and creator work, making reproducibility easier when metadata is present.
License fields and flags such as commercial use, derivatives, attribution, and different-license permissions help users evaluate model compatibility.
Civitai’s creator program can let eligible creators earn from model and generation activity, subject to current rules and licensing.
gettingStarted: Create an account at civitai.com and search by model type, base model, tags, creator, rating, or popularity.
Open a model version and inspect its license, base model, files, hash, sample prompts, trained words, and safety/NSFW labels before downloading.
Download the model or LoRA to a compatible local/hosted image-generation UI and follow that runtime’s installation and VRAM requirements.
Reproduce a sample using the displayed prompt and metadata, then adjust weights, sampler, resolution, and references in your generation tool.
When publishing, include the model/version and prompt metadata where required, credit creators, and respect the model’s exact license.
For development, use the public REST API for metadata/download discovery with bounded requests; do not assume it is an image-generation inference API.
usageNotes: Civitai is a marketplace/community catalog, not a guarantee that every model is safe, accurate, legal, maintained, or compatible with your runtime.
Every model version can have its own license. Check commercial-use, attribution, derivatives, and redistribution terms before shipping generated work or a product.
NSFW and mature content may exist and visibility/safety controls can vary; apply age, moderation, and workplace policies before browsing or integrating.
Downloaded model files are untrusted binaries/weights: scan files, prefer verified hashes, isolate runtimes, and avoid executing unknown code or extensions.
The public REST API primarily exposes catalog metadata and downloads; current community documentation does not establish a general hosted generation API for arbitrary prompts.
Images and prompts can contain personal or copyrighted material; review privacy, consent, takedown, and platform rules before uploading.
Local generation costs GPU/storage and model compatibility varies by base architecture, format, and frontend.
priceDetails: Core model discovery and community features are generally free; optional creator support, generation credits, or marketplace features may vary. Model licenses are set per model/version, not globally by Civitai.
install: Open https://civitai.com/ to browse, then download a compatible model into your chosen local or hosted Stable Diffusion frontend. API reference: https://github.com/civitai/civitai-developer-docs.
start: Search a model, inspect its version/license/samples, download it to a compatible generator, then reproduce and refine using the listed prompt metadata.

name: Canva Magic Studio
description: Canva’s integrated AI design suite for generating and editing copy, images, graphics, video, presentations, documents, and interactive content inside Visual Suite.
bestFor: Marketers, educators, creators, and teams producing social posts, presentations, videos, documents, ads, and campaign variants quickly.
Non-designers who want prompt-to-layout suggestions plus manual visual editing, templates, stock assets, and brand controls in one workspace.
Teams applying Brand Kits, brand voice, approved media, collaboration, and batch transformations across many designs.
Creators combining Magic Design, Magic Write, Magic Media, Magic Animate, background tools, translation, resize, and Canva AI features.
strengths: Magic Design analyzes a prompt, uploaded media, text, or idea and recommends editable layouts for presentations, social posts, video, and documents.
Magic Write drafts, summarizes, expands, rewrites, and adapts copy to a team’s Brand Voice; it can also help write prompts and captions.
Magic Media generates images, graphics, and short videos from text or images, while Canva AI Video can generate longer clips with sound on eligible access.
Magic Animate applies animations and transitions automatically; Magic Resize and Translate adapt designs for multiple formats and languages.
Brand Kits, approved assets, shared templates, real-time collaboration, and Visual Suite support consistent team production.
Canva’s app ecosystem can include partner models such as DALL·E, Imagen, or Leonardo-powered tools; availability and terms vary by app and region.
gettingStarted: Create or open a Canva design and launch Magic Studio, Magic Design, Magic Write, or Magic Media from the editor.
Describe the audience, channel, format, objective, tone, brand, and source content; or upload your own images/videos and ask Magic Design for layouts.
Review the generated draft, apply the appropriate Brand Kit/Brand Voice, then edit text, spacing, visuals, timing, and accessibility manually.
Use Magic Media for image/video/graphic generation and the editor for background removal, Magic Grab, erase, blend, animate, resize, or translate.
Collaborate with comments and roles, convert the result into a reusable template, and export/publish to the target channel after QA.
For high-volume work, use Canva’s batch/at-scale features where included and verify that generated assets, brand rules, and permissions remain correct.
usageNotes: Free and paid Canva plans provide different AI limits, model access, stock assets, Brand Kit capabilities, and export features; check the live plan for your region.
Magic Design recommends and arranges content; it does not generate video from scratch—video generation is handled by Magic Media or Canva AI Video.
AI output may contain incorrect text, facts, faces, logos, or visual artifacts; review claims, rights, accessibility, and brand compliance before publishing.
Partner AI apps in Canva have their own model terms, data handling, and usage limits; verify them before sending confidential content.
Brand Voice and some at-scale capabilities require Pro/Teams/Enterprise access; shared brand assets and generated designs are visible according to workspace permissions.
Commercial and licensing rights depend on Canva content licenses, generated asset type, and connected apps; do not assume every stock or AI element is unrestricted.
Cloud account access is required; no general public Magic Studio API was verified in the reviewed official materials.
priceDetails: Freemium Canva plans with plan- and region-specific AI usage limits. Pro, Teams, and Enterprise add larger AI allowances, Brand Kits/Voice, premium assets, collaboration, and at-scale tools; consult Canva’s current pricing page.
install: Open https://www.canva.com/ or use the Canva web/mobile apps; Magic Studio is built into the editor and requires no separate installation.
start: Open a design, choose Magic Design/Write/Media from the editor, provide a prompt or source media, review the draft, then refine and export.

name: Microsoft Designer
description: Microsoft’s AI-assisted design and image-editing app for creating graphics, invitations, stickers, collages, banners, and polished visuals from text or uploaded media.
bestFor: Quick social posts, greeting cards, invitations, banners, stickers, collages, and personal graphics.
Users who want prompt-to-image/design generation plus a simple canvas for manual refinement.
Microsoft 365 users creating or editing images from Word, PowerPoint, Photos, or Copilot workflows.
Lightweight photo cleanup: erase objects, remove/blur backgrounds, upscale, frame, and rewrite design text.
strengths: Text prompts generate custom images and editable designs, while example tiles help users start from common card/banner formats.
Generative Erase removes selected objects or regions with quick-select or brush masks; background removal/blur, framing, and upscaling support photo cleanup.
Generate Text and Rewrite create or refine copy inside a design, and Brand Kits can suggest a logo, voice, fonts, and colors for consistent personal branding.
Designer is integrated with Microsoft apps and Copilot workflows; mobile apps and the web app provide access across devices.
AI-edited/generated files include C2PA content credentials to signal provenance, with responsible-AI filters and abuse monitoring.
Free access is available with a Microsoft account; higher-frequency use may require a subscription or Copilot/Microsoft 365 entitlement.
gettingStarted: Open https://designer.microsoft.com/ and sign in with a Microsoft account, or use Designer from supported Microsoft apps.
Choose Create with AI, select a design type, and describe the audience, message, dimensions, visual style, and required text.
Review generated variants, apply or create a Brand Kit, then open the canvas to edit text, images, spacing, colors, and layout.
Use Edit with AI for erase, background, upscale, framing, or other image refinements; review every change against the source photo.
Download or share the final design after checking text, rights, accessibility, and whether the intended use is personal or commercial.
For Word/PowerPoint, use Copilot image creation where eligible; confirm that your Copilot Pro or Microsoft 365 subscription unlocks the feature.
usageNotes: Designer is licensed for personal, non-commercial use with a consumer Microsoft account according to the current FAQ; commercial/organization workflows require the applicable Microsoft 365 or enterprise terms.
AI features require internet access and a signed-in account; available prompts, credits, languages, and output limits vary by region and entitlement.
Microsoft collects prompts and model responses for safety monitoring and service improvement under its privacy statement; avoid confidential content unless your organization approves it.
Generated text in images may be misspelled or in the wrong language; manually proofread names, dates, logos, and legal copy.
Content credentials identify AI-generated or edited images, but they do not prove factual accuracy, ownership, or permission to use source media.
Partner or Copilot integrations can have separate data handling and subscription requirements; review permissions before connecting accounts.
No general public Designer API was verified in the reviewed official materials; do not promise programmatic access.
priceDetails: Free with a Microsoft account for personal use; more frequent AI creation or Microsoft Word/PowerPoint workflows may require Copilot Pro or Microsoft 365. Limits and entitlements vary by region and plan.
install: Open https://designer.microsoft.com/ or install the official Microsoft Designer mobile app; supported Microsoft apps may expose Designer through Copilot.
start: Sign in, choose a design type, describe it with a prompt or upload media, review variants, edit on the canvas, then download/share.

name: Figma
description: Collaborative design platform spanning Figma Design, FigJam, Slides, Dev Mode, Make, Sites, and Draw, with AI for ideation, editing, prototyping, and code handoff.
bestFor: Product and interface design with shared components, variables, prototypes, design systems, and real-time collaboration.
Designers using AI to generate layouts, copy, images, feedback, design-system applications, and repetitive canvas edits.
Teams turning Figma designs into functional prototypes or web apps through Figma Make and annotated iteration.
Developers inspecting designs in Dev Mode, using code snippets/plugins, variables, and design-to-code handoff.
strengths: The Figma agent is a conversational canvas assistant that can generate designs, make edits, apply a design system, give feedback, and create plugins or shaders.
Figma Make turns prompts and existing designs into functional prototypes, interactive UI, and web-app explorations with iterative preview.
AI image tools can generate/edit images, remove backgrounds, improve resolution, expand images, isolate objects, and run multiple tasks across frames.
Figma spans Design, FigJam, Slides, Make, Sites, Buzz, Draw, and Dev Mode, keeping ideation, design, collaboration, and handoff connected.
Dev Mode exposes code-oriented inspection, annotations, custom code snippets, codegen plugins, and API-backed design-system workflows.
REST/plugin/widget APIs, variables, libraries, permissions, version history, comments, and team workspaces support extensible production workflows.
gettingStarted: Create a Figma account and open a Design file, FigJam board, Slides deck, or Make project based on the deliverable.
Use the Figma agent or Actions to describe the user, platform, content, layout, constraints, and existing design system.
Review generated frames, copy, images, components, and prototype interactions; apply real content and validate responsive/accessibility states.
Use Figma Make when you need a functional prototype or web-app exploration, attaching relevant Figma designs and iterating through the preview chat.
Switch to Dev Mode for measurements, annotations, variables, code snippets, and handoff; use plugins/API only with approved scopes.
Share for comments or co-editing, maintain version history, and prepare a source-of-truth library before implementation.
usageNotes: Figma has Starter, Professional, Organization, and Enterprise plans with Full, Dev, Collab, and free View seats; product access depends on plan and seat type.
Figma agent is in beta and available across plans, but making edits requires a Full seat and edit access; standalone AI tools generally require paid Full seats.
Figma AI uses shared credits across products; current documented examples range from 2–16 credits per image operation, while Figma Make cost varies by model, complexity, and context.
AI output may be misleading or wrong; verify content, interaction logic, responsive behavior, accessibility, security, and code before implementation.
Figma Make prototypes may need a backend for authentication, persistence, secrets, or multi-browser state; do not treat a preview as production architecture.
Workspace admins can disable AI and control plugins, libraries, sharing, and data access; review permissions before attaching proprietary designs.
Cloud collaboration is account-based; no fully offline AI runtime was verified, and API/plugin tokens must be scoped and protected.
priceDetails: Freemium Starter plan plus Professional, Organization, and Enterprise tiers. Seat type (Full, Dev, Collab, View) controls product access; AI credits and some Figma Make features are plan-dependent. See current Figma pricing for seat rates.
install: Open https://www.figma.com/ or install the official desktop app. Developers can use plugins, widgets, REST API, Dev Mode, and Figma Make from supported plans.
start: Create a file, open Actions/Figma AI or Figma Make, describe the desired design/prototype, then review, refine, collaborate, and hand off in Dev Mode.

name: Uizard
description: AI-powered UI design and prototyping workspace that turns text prompts, screenshots, and hand-drawn wireframes into editable multi-screen interfaces.
bestFor: Rapid app and website ideation before engineering or high-fidelity design work.
Founders, product managers, and designers creating mobile/web mockups, wireframes, prototypes, and user-flow concepts.
Teams transforming existing screenshots or sketches into editable screens and reusable components.
Organizations applying themes, design tokens, custom templates, and developer handoff to keep generated UI consistent.
strengths: Autodesigner generates multi-screen editable mockups from a short text brief, with a selectable theme and UX-oriented structure.
Screenshot Scanner converts app or web screenshots into editable UI designs; Wireframe Scanner turns sketches into digital wireframes.
Design Assistant can extract colors, typography, components, and styling from inspiration images to create a reusable theme.
Wireframe mode switches between low-fidelity structure and high-fidelity themed mockups without rebuilding screens.
Drag-and-drop editing, components, interactions, transitions, collaboration, templates, and unlimited viewers/commenters support review workflows.
Pro/Business plans add React/CSS developer handoff, private projects, larger AI quotas, custom brand kits, and design-system controls.
gettingStarted: Create a Uizard account and start a project from Autodesigner, a template, a blank canvas, Screenshot Scanner, or Wireframe Scanner.
Describe the product, target users, platform, key screens, content, and desired visual style; let Autodesigner generate a first multi-screen project.
Review the structure, replace placeholder copy and imagery, and use theme/wireframe controls to explore low- and high-fidelity directions.
Upload screenshots or sketches when reverse-engineering an existing flow, then correct detected components and interactions manually.
Add prototype links, transitions, comments, and real content; validate responsive states, accessibility, and user flows with stakeholders.
Use React/CSS handoff or export JPG/PNG/PDF where your plan supports it, then treat the result as a design starting point for implementation.
usageNotes: Free currently includes 3 AI generations/month, 2 projects, 5 screens/project, and 10 templates; Pro is listed at $12/month annually with 500 generations, and Business at $39/month with 5,000.
Enterprise plans can add unlimited AI generations, teams, design-system setup, custom billing, and data SLAs; verify current pricing and seat terms.
AI-generated UI is a concept, not production code: verify information architecture, states, accessibility, content, performance, and security before implementation.
Screenshot/Sketch scanning may miss semantics, responsive behavior, hidden states, or interaction logic; manually reconstruct critical flows.
Private projects, custom brand kits, export resolution, and developer handoff are plan-dependent.
Cloud account access is required; avoid uploading confidential product screenshots or user data without reviewing workspace privacy and retention terms.
No public API was verified in the reviewed official materials; use documented exports/handoff instead of promising programmatic generation.
priceDetails: Freemium. Free: 3 AI generations/month and 2 projects. Pro: $12/month billed annually with 500 AI generations; Business: $39/month with 5,000. Enterprise is custom and adds governance/design-system features.
install: Open https://uizard.io/ and sign up; no local installation is required for the web editor.
start: Create a project with Autodesigner or upload a screenshot/sketch, review generated screens, apply a theme, and add prototype interactions.

name: Framer
description: AI-powered visual website builder for creating, editing, localizing, and publishing responsive marketing sites without a traditional code-first workflow.
bestFor: Landing pages, portfolios, startup and agency marketing sites
Designers and teams that want editable AI-generated layouts instead of locked templates
CMS-driven content hubs and multilingual websites
Publishing production sites with managed hosting, SEO, forms, and analytics in one workspace
strengths: Framer AI agents generate editable pages, sections, copy, and visuals directly on the canvas
Visual responsive editing with components, breakpoints, interactions, and animation controls
Built-in CMS for dynamic collections, detail pages, filters, and reusable content structures
Localization supports automatic translation, regional locales, RTL layouts, and automatic locale routing
Managed hosting includes SSL, CDN delivery, redirects, performance optimization, and custom domains on paid plans
Built-in SEO controls, forms, privacy-first cookie-free analytics, and custom code for tags such as GA4 or Meta Pixel
Collaboration features include shared editing, staging, branching, previews, and role-based access on eligible plans
gettingStarted: Create a Framer project from a prompt, blank canvas, template, or existing concept.
Describe the audience, goal, visual direction, and required pages to the AI agent.
Review and refine generated structure, copy, assets, components, typography, and responsive breakpoints on the canvas.
Add CMS collections, forms, SEO metadata, analytics, custom code, and localization when the site needs production features.
Preview across breakpoints, connect a domain on a paid plan, and publish through Framer hosting.
usageNotes: AI output is a starting direction: verify copy, links, accessibility, performance, legal text, and mobile behavior before publishing.
Free projects can use a Framer subdomain; custom domains require a paid site plan.
Pricing and limits vary by plan, billing cycle, editor seats, AI credits, CMS collections, locales, and add-ons.
Framer Analytics is privacy-first and cookie-free, so its numbers may differ from Google Analytics.
Use custom code for third-party scripts carefully and test consent, security, and page performance.
An account is required; normal work happens in the cloud through the Framer web app.
priceDetails: Free plan available with a Framer domain and limited resources. Current listed paid plans include Basic at $10/month and Pro at $30/month when billed monthly; Enterprise is custom. AI credits, editor seats, localization, advanced hosting, and A/B testing can add separate charges. Confirm current limits and billing cycle on the pricing page.
install: No local installation is required for the hosted workflow. Open Framer in a browser and sign in; a desktop app download is also offered for supported workflows.
start: Open https://www.framer.com/ai/ to start with an AI-generated site or https://www.framer.com/ to create a project.

name: Relume
description: AI website planning and design system platform that turns a brief into sitemaps, wireframes, copy, and style directions, with exports for Figma, Webflow, and Relume Publish.
bestFor: Rapidly scoping marketing and client websites from a business brief
Generating a complete sitemap and responsive wireframes before visual design
Agencies and freelancers standardizing projects with Relume components and style guides
Exporting a structured concept to Figma or Webflow, or publishing through Relume Publish
strengths: AI sitemap generation maps business goals and required pages into a navigable site structure
Wireframe generation uses Relume’s component library to create responsive page sections quickly
AI copywriting can draft section-level content while keeping page context in view
Style guide concepts help establish typography, colors, buttons, and visual direction early
Official Figma library and Webflow export support smoother handoff to production workflows
Relume Publish can host sites with staging URLs, custom domains, readiness checks, and Lighthouse scores
Export tools can produce project scope and pricing spreadsheets for client estimation
gettingStarted: Create a Relume project and describe the company, audience, site goals, and must-have pages.
Generate and review the sitemap; rename, reorder, add, or remove pages before wireframing.
Generate wireframes for selected pages, then refine sections, responsive layouts, and copy.
Create or adjust a style guide and apply components consistently across the project.
Export to Figma or Webflow for implementation, or use Relume Publish when you want hosted output.
usageNotes: Treat generated sitemaps, copy, and layouts as drafts; validate information architecture and content with stakeholders.
Relume is strongest for marketing and content sites, not highly bespoke application logic or complex backend products.
Exported designs still need implementation QA for responsive behavior, accessibility, SEO, forms, and integrations.
Relume Publish hosting and account AI usage are separate plans; check pageview, AI, and domain limits before launch.
A free address on relume-staging.io is available for published sites; custom domains require the appropriate hosting plan.
An account is required and the normal workflow runs in the cloud through the web app.
priceDetails: Relume offers a free trial/free access with paid workspace tiers; current pricing and AI capacity can change. Relume Publish hosting is billed separately from account AI usage, with Free and paid launch plans. Check the official pricing and account Plans & hosting screens for current limits, billing cycle, pageviews, and export entitlements.
install: No local installation is required. Open Relume in a browser and sign in; optional Figma and Webflow integrations are used during export.
start: Open https://www.relume.ai/ to create a project, generate a sitemap, and explore the Site Builder.

name: Visily
description: AI-powered UI design workspace that turns prompts, screenshots, sketches, and diagrams into editable wireframes, mockups, prototypes, and developer-ready handoff assets.
bestFor: Product teams creating web or mobile flows without starting from a blank canvas
Turning screenshots, sketches, or text ideas into editable UI screens
Fast prototyping, user-flow presentations, and stakeholder review
Handing designs to Figma and developers with CSS inspection
strengths: Multimodal input accepts text, screenshots, hand-drawn sketches, and flow diagrams
AI can generate screens, components, prototypes, diagrams, themes, images, and code
Large template and component library accelerates common web-app and mobile patterns
Interactive prototypes, comments, sharing, workspaces, and permissions support collaboration
Figma plugin exports designs for pixel-level refinement; JPG, PNG, and PDF exports support documentation
CSS inspection exposes exact style values for implementation and developer handoff
Starter, Pro, and Business plans provide different board, collaboration, export, and AI-credit limits
gettingStarted: Create a workspace and start a board from a prompt, template, screenshot, or sketch.
Ask Visily AI to generate screens or components, then edit layers, layout, content, and theme visually.
Connect screens into an interactive prototype and use comments or share links for review.
Inspect CSS values and export to Figma for production refinement, or export PNG, JPG, or PDF deliverables.
Track AI credits in workspace settings and upgrade or top up when the team needs more capacity.
usageNotes: Generated screens are editable concepts; validate flows, content, accessibility, responsive behavior, and edge states before implementation.
Free Starter limits boards, credits, exports, and collaboration; Pro and Business increase capacity and remove watermarks.
AI credits are consumed per feature and reset monthly; unused monthly credits do not roll over.
Figma export is available through Visily’s plugin/workflow; exported designs still require component and interaction QA.
An account is required and the standard workflow runs in the cloud through the web app.
priceDetails: Starter is free forever with limited boards, AI/template credits, and export capacity. Current public materials list Pro at about $11–$14 per editor/month and Business at $29/month, with Enterprise custom pricing; verify current billing, seats, credits, and limits on Visily’s pricing screen.
install: No local installation is required. Use Visily in a browser; install the optional Visily Figma plugin when exporting designs to Figma.
start: Open https://www.visily.ai/ and create a free workspace.

name: Lummi
description: AI-powered visual asset library and creation suite for royalty-free photos, illustrations, 3D visuals, image generation, retouching, and creative effects.
bestFor: Finding distinctive stock visuals for websites, products, campaigns, and social content
Generating or retouching images when a stock search is not enough
Designers who need photos, illustrations, and 3D assets in one searchable library
Creating collections and quickly testing reframe, background removal, duotone, or similar-image variations
strengths: Search and browse photos, illustrations, and 3D assets by subject, style, or vibe
AI Create and Retouch tools generate and modify visuals using ByteDance Seedream models
Reframe, upscale, remove backgrounds, retouch, duotone, and similar-image tools speed production edits
Free library images can be used for personal and commercial projects without attribution under Lummi’s license
Collections, favorites, profiles, and activity history help organize reusable assets
Paid plans unlock watermark-free premium downloads, higher resolutions, AI tools, and video generation
Public API supports image search, filters, downloads, effects, similar images, collections, and creator data by request
gettingStarted: Open Lummi and search by subject, visual style, or vibe, or choose Create for a new generated image.
Preview an asset and save it to a collection; check the license before publishing or redistributing work.
Use Reframe, Retouch, Remove Background, Duotone, or Similar to adapt the selected image.
Download the required resolution and keep the source link or collection reference in your project notes.
Request API access separately if you need programmatic search, downloads, or generation.
usageNotes: Most library images are free for commercial and personal use with no attribution, but you may not resell them or build a competing stock service.
Free access may include watermarks, resolution, and generation limits; verify current account limits before a production batch.
Paid AI credits and generation speed vary by Pro or Max plan and can change over time.
Review faces, logos, trademarks, and model-generated content for rights and brand safety before publishing.
An account is required for saving, downloads, and the normal cloud workflow.
priceDetails: Free browsing and a free image library are available. Current listed plans show Pro at $15/month monthly or $10/month billed yearly, and Max at $48/month monthly or $32/month billed yearly; plan features include watermark-free downloads, AI tools, credits, and video generation. Confirm current pricing at checkout.
install: No local installation is required. Use Lummi in a browser; API access is requested separately through the developer page.
start: Open https://www.lummi.ai/ to search the library or create a visual.

name: Runway
description: Cloud creative suite for generating and editing AI images, video, and audio, with browser workflows and an asynchronous developer API.
bestFor: Short-form text-to-video, image-to-video, and generative image experiments
Creators and production teams iterating on cinematic clips, visual effects, and social assets
API pipelines that need asynchronous generation tasks and downloadable outputs
Teams that want shared workspaces, comments, skills, and pooled generation credits
strengths: Runway models support text-to-video, image-to-video, image generation, video editing, and generative audio workflows
Web app provides prompt-driven creation with model, duration, ratio, and asset controls
Gen-4 family and third-party model access vary by plan and continue to evolve
Shared workspaces support collaboration, comments, role management, and pooled credits
Developer API uses asynchronous tasks with documented polling/wait patterns and image inputs
Free plan provides a one-time credit allotment and asset storage for trying supported tools
Paid plans provide larger monthly credit pools; Max includes all models and one-month credit rollover
gettingStarted: Create a Runway account and open the web app, or request an API key for server-side integrations.
Choose a supported image, video, or audio model and write a concise prompt describing subject, motion, style, and camera intent.
Generate a short draft, review moderation and quality, then iterate with references, edits, or upscaling.
Track credit usage in Plans & Billing; keep production keys in server or CI secrets, never browser code.
Download approved outputs and document model, prompt, rights, and provenance for your production workflow.
usageNotes: Generation is asynchronous and consumes credits based on model, duration, quality, and output count.
Free credits are a one-time deposit; paid monthly credits generally expire on the billing date, while purchased credits do not expire.
Runway app credits and Runway API credits are separate balances and cannot be used interchangeably.
Check current model availability, content policy, public-figure restrictions, and commercial rights before release.
Use bounded retries and backoff for API rate limits, and validate generated media for artifacts, continuity, audio, and licensing.
priceDetails: Free plan includes 125 one-time credits and 5 GB storage. Current help pages list 625 monthly credits for Standard, 2,250 for Pro/Unlimited, 9,500 for Max, and 6,900 per Team seat; exact subscription prices and model access vary by billing and may change.
install: No local installation is needed for the web app. For API integrations, install the official SDK in your server project and keep RUNWAYML_API_SECRET private.
start: Open https://runwayml.com/ for the creative app or https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/ for API documentation.

name: Kling AI
description: Text and image to video generator with motion and camera controls.
bestFor: Text-to-video and image-to-video generation through a hosted API.
Reference-driven clips using start and end frames, image lists, prompts, and multi-shot storyboards.
Projects that need selectable model versions, aspect ratios, duration, generation mode, sound, or 4K-capable output.
strengths: The official API exposes image-to-video at `POST /v1/videos/image2video` and omni-video at `POST /v1/videos/omni-video`.
Requests can use Base64 images or image URLs, with documented size, dimension, format, and aspect-ratio constraints.
Supports positive and negative prompts, model selection, duration, mode, aspect ratio, sound settings, multi-shot generation, and custom storyboard prompts.
Generation is asynchronous and returns a task ID with `submitted`, `processing`, `succeed`, or `failed` status values.
Completion callbacks and customer-defined external task IDs are available for tracking jobs.
gettingStarted: Create an API credential through the official Kling AI developer flow and keep it in a server-side secret.
Choose a documented model and submit a small text-to-video or image-to-video request with the required Authorization header.
Store the returned task ID and poll the corresponding task status endpoint or configure a callback URL.
Start with a short duration and standard mode, then add reference frames, sound, multi-shot settings, or higher-quality modes after validation.
usageNotes: Keep Authorization credentials out of browser code, public repositories, logs, and client-provided prompts.
Image inputs must meet the documented format, size, dimension, and aspect-ratio requirements; some reference-image controls are mutually exclusive.
A prompt can be limited to 2,500 characters depending on the endpoint; validate input before submission.
Treat task status as asynchronous and handle both failed jobs and callback retries in production.
Model names, duration options, resolution modes, and pricing vary by endpoint; verify the selected model's current reference page.

name: Pika
description: Video generation tool focused on short clips and creative effects.
bestFor: Short cinematic text-to-video and image-to-video clips for social, advertising, and creative development.
Style exploration, look development, and multi-shot sequences using Pika and other models exposed through the Pika API.
Media-generation pipelines that need video, image, audio, music, and 3D model endpoints behind one REST API.
strengths: The official API uses concrete REST endpoints such as `POST /v1/media/{vendor}/{model}/{function}` and asynchronous jobs.
A single Pika API key can access video, image, audio, music, and 3D models, with a public model catalog and per-model references.
The workflow returns a job ID, supports status polling, and exposes a separate content endpoint for the result URL.
Public reference media can be passed by URL; local files can be uploaded through a presigned URL workflow.
Pika 2.5 Keyframe supports 2–5 ordered keyframe images, transition prompts, 720p or 1080p output, and configurable transition duration.
gettingStarted: Create a Pika developer account and API key, then store it in an environment variable.
Choose a model page and copy its exact endpoint and request schema; for a basic example, start with Pika text-to-video.
Send JSON over HTTPS with `X-API-Key` and store the returned request ID.
Poll `GET /v1/media/jobs/{request_id}` until the job completes, then fetch `GET /v1/media/jobs/{request_id}/content` for the output URL.
For local reference files, request a presigned upload URL, upload the bytes, and pass the returned hosted URL to the model.
usageNotes: Never expose `X-API-Key` in browser code or other client-side applications; call the API from a server.
Use the exact model-specific endpoint and parameters because capabilities, resolutions, durations, and pricing differ by model.
Generation is asynchronous; handle `queued`, `running`, `completed`, and `failed` states and retain the job ID for recovery.
Presigned upload URLs are temporary and the documented upload URL expires after five minutes; upload the exact content type and byte size requested.
Official model guidance notes that these tools are not intended for frame-exact rotoscoping, feature-length rendering, pixel-perfect compositing, or precise on-screen text.

name: Luma Dream Machine
description: Luma's video model for text and image to video with camera motion controls.
bestFor: Programmatic image and video generation through the official Luma API and SDK.
Prompt-driven video, image-to-video, reference-guided generation, video editing, and reframing workflows.
Applications that need asynchronous generation jobs with model, aspect-ratio, duration, resolution, and output controls.
strengths: The official Python SDK provides typed synchronous and asynchronous access to the Luma REST API.
`client.generations.create()` accepts a prompt, generation type, model, aspect ratio, image references, source media, video options, and optional end-user ID.
Documented generation types include image, image edit, video, video edit, video reframe, and layering.
Video generation supports model-specific duration and resolution options, including a documented Ray 3.2 example using 5 seconds at 1080p.
`client.generations.get()` exposes queued, processing, completed, and failed states, including output URLs or failure details.
gettingStarted: Install the official Luma Agents Python package and configure the API credentials required by the SDK.
Initialize the client and submit a small generation with `client.generations.create()` using `type="video"` and a documented model.
Store the generation ID and poll `client.generations.get(generation.id)` until the state is completed or failed.
When completed, download the media from the output URL; when failed, record the failure code and reason for troubleshooting.
usageNotes: Generation is asynchronous; do not assume the create response contains final media output.
Validate model-specific options such as duration, resolution, aspect ratio, and reference-media formats against the current API reference.
Use an opaque `user_id` when the integration needs to associate generations with end users without putting personal data in prompts.
Keep API credentials server-side and add bounded polling, timeout handling, and failure recovery around long-running jobs.
Output URLs are returned after completion; store or process them according to the current retention and access behavior documented by Luma.

name: Synthesia
description: Generates presenter-led videos from scripts with AI avatars and voiceovers.
bestFor: Programmatically creating presenter-led business videos from reusable Synthesia templates.
Personalized, branded, and multilingual video generation at scale through an API.
Production workflows that need private-by-default videos, test renders, callbacks, and status retrieval.
strengths: The public API provides a template-based video creation endpoint at `https://api.synthesia.io/v2/videos/fromTemplate`.
Template generation accepts template data, title, description, folder, CTA settings, callback ID, brand kit, visibility, and test mode.
Test videos are free, do not count toward quota, and include a watermark; normal visibility defaults to private.
The API supports translation and video generation from XLIFF content through `/v2/translate/manual`.
Webhooks can notify an integration about video events, and the API provides video retrieval by ID.
gettingStarted: Obtain a Synthesia API key and store it in a server-side secret.
Select or create a template and collect its template ID and required template data.
Create a test video first with the template endpoint, then inspect the returned video ID and generated result.
Retrieve the video by ID or configure a webhook endpoint with a signing secret for asynchronous notifications.
Move to normal generation only after checking visibility, brand kit, CTA, quota, and review requirements.
usageNotes: Requests require the Authorization API key header; never expose it in browser code, repositories, or logs.
Validate template data against the selected template because required fields are template-specific.
Keep test and production generation paths separate; test output is watermarked even though it does not count toward quota.
Webhook secrets should be kept private and used to verify incoming events before updating downstream systems.
The API exposes 400, 403, 404, and server-error responses; handle invalid input, wrong credentials, missing videos, and transient failures explicitly.

name: HeyGen
description: Avatar video platform with translation and lip-sync dubbing for marketing and training.
bestFor: Generating presenter-led avatar videos from scripts, selected avatars, and voices through an API.
Product integrations that need branded video-agent generation, multilingual translation, or asynchronous video workflows.
Applications combining avatar, voice, style, brand-kit, orientation, file attachments, and completion callbacks.
strengths: The official API authenticates requests with the `X-Api-Key` header and exposes avatar and video endpoints under `api.heygen.com`.
`POST /v3/videos` can create a direct avatar video using an avatar ID, voice ID, and script.
`POST /v3/video-agents` accepts a 1–10,000 character prompt plus optional avatar, voice, style, brand, orientation, file, callback, and incognito settings.
The API supports video translation tasks with a dedicated translation-status endpoint.
Asynchronous results can be tracked by polling the video status until `completed` or `failed`, then reading the video URL.
gettingStarted: Create a HeyGen API key and store it in an environment variable such as `HEYGEN_API_KEY`.
List available avatars and voices, choose a look and voice, then submit a small request to `POST /v3/videos`.
For prompt-driven generation, use `POST /v3/video-agents` with a focused prompt and optional brand or style configuration.
Store the returned video or task ID and poll the appropriate status endpoint until the job completes or fails.
Review the generated video before publishing, especially when using custom files, translated speech, or brand assets.
usageNotes: Keep `X-Api-Key` server-side; do not place it in browser bundles, public repositories, URLs, or logs.
Video-agent prompts are documented as 1–10,000 characters; validate length and attachments before submission.
Use callback URLs for completion or failure notifications, but verify incoming webhook requests in your application.
Translation and video generation are asynchronous; use bounded polling and handle both failed tasks and missing output URLs.
The `incognito_mode` option disables memory injection and extraction for that session when privacy requires it.
Avatar, voice, style, brand-kit, file, language, and translation availability can depend on the account and current API version.

Start a project and choose a text, image, or video workflow; describe subject, action, camera, style, duration, and aspect ratio.
Generate a short clip, then refine it with references, scene sequencing, extension, edits, audio, or the Flow Agent.
Review active model, resolution, watermark, and credit cost in prompt settings before confirming generation.
Organize approved clips into scenes and export/download media for editing or delivery.
usageNotes: Features, models, regions, and limits vary by Google AI subscription tier and can change frequently.

Best experienced on desktop Chromium; the standard workflow is cloud-based and requires a Google account.
priceDetails: Current Google Flow page lists a free tier with 50 daily credits, Google AI Plus at $4.99/month, Pro at $19.99/month, and Ultra tiers at $99.99 or $199.99/month, with different monthly credits and feature limits. Prices, regions, and credits are subject to change; verify the live plan page before subscribing.

start: Open https://labs.google/fx/tools/flow/ and create a project with a Google account.

name: Jan
description: Open-source, local-first AI desktop app for running models privately, connecting cloud providers, using MCP tools, and exposing OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible APIs.
bestFor: Private offline chat, document work, coding, and agent workflows on a personal computer
Developers who need a local OpenAI-compatible server for apps and coding tools
Users combining downloaded GGUF models with optional cloud providers and MCP connectors
strengths: Runs local models through llama.cpp or MLX and can work fully offline after model download
Built-in Hub helps find models and shows hardware fit before downloading
Includes Projects, Assistants, Agents, Cowork preview, and MCP connectors for tool-enabled workflows
Local API supports OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` and Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoints
gettingStarted: Download Jan for Windows, macOS, or Linux and open the desktop app.
Open Hub, choose a model that fits your hardware, download it, and select it in a chat.
For local integrations, open Settings > Local API Server, set an API key, and start the server at `http://127.0.0.1:1337`.
Use Projects, Assistants, Agents, or MCP connectors to organize files and tool-enabled tasks; add cloud providers only when needed.
usageNotes: Jan Desktop is free and open source under Apache 2.0; local models run without a cloud account or usage fees.
The local API requires a configured non-empty API key for requests even though inference stays on your computer.
Custom providers can target any OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoint, including Ollama, vLLM, LocalAI, LiteLLM, and Bedrock proxies.
Model performance depends on hardware, runtime, quantization, and context settings; review each model’s license before redistribution.
Cloud providers require their own credentials and may incur separate costs; local conversations remain offline when using local models.
priceDetails: Jan Desktop is free and open source. Local inference has no Jan usage fee; connected cloud providers, model licenses, and hosted endpoints may charge separately.
install: Download installers for macOS, Windows, or Linux from https://www.jan.ai/download. The separate Jan CLI can launch agents or serve models from a terminal.
start: Launch Jan, download a model from Hub, select it in Chat, and start a conversation; use Settings > Local API Server for integrations.
commands: jan launch
jan serve [MODEL_ID]

name: GPT4All
description: Open-source desktop app and Python library for running downloadable GGUF language models locally, chatting with private files, and exposing a local OpenAI-compatible API.
bestFor: Private offline chat and retrieval-augmented conversations over local documents
Running compact 3–13B models on consumer hardware without a hosted account
Developers embedding local inference or LocalDocs context into applications
strengths: Desktop model browser downloads Hugging Face GGUF files and shows approximate RAM, size, quantization, and license information
LocalDocs indexes folders with on-device embeddings and injects relevant snippets into chats
Optional local API server exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints at `http://localhost:4891/v1`
Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux with CPU, GPU, or Apple Metal device options
gettingStarted: Download and launch GPT4All Desktop for Windows, macOS, or Linux.
Open Models > Add Model, choose a GGUF model that fits your RAM, and download it from the catalog.
Start a chat, or create a LocalDocs collection from a folder and attach it as a private source.
For integrations, enable Settings > Application > Advanced > Local API Server and point an OpenAI client to `http://localhost:4891/v1`.
usageNotes: Local model execution is free and can work offline; remote provider APIs are optional and send prompts to the selected provider.
The local API listens on localhost over HTTP and is disabled by default; do not expose it to a network without separate access controls.
Model licenses vary by uploader and model family, so check the license before commercial use or redistribution.
LocalDocs supports text-oriented files such as TXT, PDF, Markdown, and reStructuredText; indexing quality depends on extraction and chunk settings.
Hardware requirements vary substantially by quantization and model size; larger models need more RAM/VRAM and storage.
priceDetails: GPT4All Desktop and its local runtime are free and open source. Optional remote model APIs, hardware, and individual model licenses may have separate terms or costs.
install: Download the desktop app from https://gpt4all.io/ or the official docs for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Python users can install the `gpt4all` package for local inference.
start: Launch GPT4All, add a model from the Explore Models screen, and begin a local chat; use Settings to enable Local API Server or LocalDocs.

name: AnythingLLM
description: Open-source local-first AI workspace for document knowledge, RAG chat, agents, MCP tools, meeting notes, and self-hosted multi-user deployments.
bestFor: Private document Q&A and research organized into persistent workspaces
Local agents that can use tools, skills, web search, and file-system actions
Teams that need a self-hosted multi-user AI workspace with permissions and white-label options
strengths: Desktop runs locally with no account, API key, token limits, or required cloud service
Document Knowledge, vector search, model selection, and workspace context support practical RAG workflows
Agents, custom skills, MCP, background jobs, meeting transcription/summaries, and file-system tools extend beyond chat
Docker/self-hosted Cloud deployments add multi-user isolation, admin controls, SSO/RBAC, custom domains, and enterprise support
gettingStarted: Download the desktop app for macOS, Windows, or Linux, or deploy the server with Docker.
Pick a local or remote LLM and embedding provider, then create a workspace for a project or knowledge base.
Add documents and let AnythingLLM index them; start with document-grounded chat before enabling agent tools.
Configure skills/MCP and workspace permissions deliberately, then expose the API only behind appropriate authentication.
usageNotes: AnythingLLM Desktop is free, open source, and local by default; cloud plans and external model providers can add separate costs.
Query mode is document-grounded, Chat mode is open-ended, and Agent mode can call skills/tools and requires a capable tool-calling model.
The Meeting Assistant records, transcribes, summarizes, and indexes meetings on-device without a bot joining the call.
Self-hosted deployments should mount only the directories agents need, protect API keys, and configure user roles and workspace deletion safeguards.
AnythingLLM supports macOS, Windows, and Linux desktop builds, Docker/server deployment, and a mobile app that can sync with desktop or cloud.
priceDetails: Desktop and self-hosting are free. AnythingLLM Cloud currently lists Basic at $50/month and Pro at $99/month, with Enterprise custom pricing; model-provider usage and infrastructure are separate.
install: Download the one-file desktop installer from https://anythingllm.com/download, or follow the Docker deployment guide at https://docs.anythingllm.com/installation.
start: Open the desktop app, choose a model, create a workspace, and add documents; server users can deploy with Docker and open the web workspace.

name: Open WebUI
description: Open-source self-hosted AI workspace that unifies Ollama and OpenAI-compatible providers with chat, RAG knowledge bases, agents, MCP tools, and team administration.
bestFor: A private browser UI for local Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, or cloud-compatible models
Document-grounded research and knowledge bases with embeddings and retrieval
Teams that need workspaces, user roles, tool permissions, API access, and self-hosted control
strengths: Protocol-oriented connections work with Ollama, OpenAI-compatible APIs, and experimental Open Responses providers
RAG supports file context, embeddings, reranking, multiple vector databases, and knowledge collections
Built-in and custom tools support function calling, MCP/OpenAPI integrations, web search, and agentic loops
Runs locally or in Docker with persistent storage; the REST API exposes chat, files, knowledge, and provider routes
gettingStarted: Deploy Open WebUI with the official Docker image or install it using the documented Python/desktop path.
Connect Ollama or another OpenAI-compatible server in Admin Settings → Connections and verify model discovery.
Create a workspace or knowledge collection, upload a few documents, and test retrieval before enabling agents.
Set a persistent `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY`, secure storage, roles, and tool permissions before inviting other users.
usageNotes: The self-hosted application is free and open source; connected cloud model providers may require their own accounts, API keys, and billing.
For OpenAI-compatible providers, chat completions are required; embeddings are needed when using that provider for RAG.
Offline mode requires pre-downloading embedding, reranking, and Whisper assets; web search and external APIs will still need network access.
Treat Workspace Tools, MCP, OpenAPI, and terminal capabilities as privileged code execution; allow only trusted tools and minimal filesystem/network access.
Use persistent secrets and pinned image versions for production, and keep user/API tokens out of browser code or public repositories.
priceDetails: Open WebUI is free and open source when self-hosted. Infrastructure and connected model/API providers are separate costs; managed hosting, if used, follows its provider’s current pricing.
install: Recommended Docker deployment is documented at https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/; native Python and desktop options are also listed in the installation guides.
start: Deploy Open WebUI, open the local web address, connect Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and select a model from the chat selector.

name: Msty
description: Privacy-focused desktop AI workspace for local and remote models, multi-model chats, knowledge stacks, web search, attachments, and prompt workflows.
bestFor: Comparing local and cloud models in one conversation workspace
Private document and knowledge-base chat with local or remote embeddings
Creators and developers who want branching chats, prompts, web research, and model controls without a mandatory account
strengths: Supports local models through its bundled Local AI service/Ollama and imports existing Ollama models
Knowledge Stacks provide RAG over documents with configurable embedding and retrieval settings
Includes split chats, branching, attachments, web search, Flowchat, personas/prompts, and image interpretation
Can connect OpenAI-compatible and major remote providers while keeping local workflows offline-friendly
gettingStarted: Download and install Msty for your operating system, then choose Setup Local AI, Add Remote Models Provider, or existing Ollama Models.
Select a model in the unified model selector and start a chat; pin frequently used models for quick access.
Create a Knowledge Stack, add documents, choose a local or remote embedding model, and test retrieval with a focused question.
Use split chats, web search, attachments, or Flowchat for larger research and content workflows.
usageNotes: Personal use is free with no sign-up required; professional or business use requires a paid license.
The official pricing page currently lists the Aurum plan at $129 per user per year and a limited lifetime-access option; check the live page for current availability.
Local AI keeps model processing on-device after downloads, while remote providers send prompts to their own APIs and require provider credentials.
Msty can share a models path with Ollama; changing that path restarts the local service, so back up or verify existing model locations first.
Treat web search, remote models, attachments, and knowledge sources according to their privacy and retention terms; review output before publishing.
priceDetails: Free plan for personal use. Professional/business licensing is paid; the official pricing page currently lists Aurum at $129 per user/year, with a limited lifetime-access option. Provider API charges are separate.
install: Download Msty from https://msty.app/ or the official download links, then follow onboarding to install Local AI or connect Ollama.
start: Open Msty, pick a local or remote provider during onboarding, select a model, and start a chat.

name: Cherry Studio
description: Open-source desktop AI client for multi-model chat, local and cloud providers, document knowledge bases, web search, image generation, translation, and MCP tools.
bestFor: Comparing multiple model responses and providers in one configurable desktop workspace
Local RAG over PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, TXT, Markdown, URLs, and sitemaps
Power users who want MCP servers, web search, exports, and local/offline model options
strengths: Supports local models through Ollama and imported GGUF files, alongside OpenAI-compatible and other cloud providers
Knowledge Base supports multiple file and URL sources, embedding models, vector search, relevance scores, and source citations
MCP integration can install and run STDIO servers such as fetch, extending chats with external tools
Includes parallel multi-model answers, custom assistants, image generation, translation, exports, and customizable chat layouts
gettingStarted: Download Cherry Studio for Windows, macOS, or Linux from the official client download page.
Add a local provider such as Ollama or configure a remote provider with its API key, then select a model.
Create a Knowledge Base, choose an embedding model, add documents or URLs, and run a retrieval test.
Configure MCP servers in Settings → MCP Server and enable only the tools required for the current conversation.
usageNotes: The desktop client is free and open source; cloud provider API usage, model licenses, and hosted services may charge separately.
Knowledge Base files and processed fragments are stored locally by default, but remote embedding or chat models can receive the selected content.
MCP setup may download bundled `uv` and `bun` binaries; review server commands and permissions before enabling them.
When using web search or URL sources, anti-scraping and login restrictions can reduce retrieval quality; verify citations and source freshness.
Cherry Studio requires Windows 8.1 or newer (Windows 7 is unsupported) and has native macOS/Linux builds.
priceDetails: Cherry Studio is free and open source. External model/API providers, hosted search, and any third-party services configured in the client have their own pricing and terms.
install: Download the desktop installer from https://docs.cherry-ai.com/cherry-studio-wen-dang/en-us/cherrystudio/download, or use the official GitHub releases.
start: Install Cherry Studio, add a local or remote provider, select a model, and start a chat; use the sidebar to create a Knowledge Base or configure MCP.

name: LocalAI
description: Open-source self-hosted AI runtime that exposes OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible APIs for text, vision, audio, image, video, embeddings, reranking, and local agents.
bestFor: Replacing hosted model endpoints with controllable local or on-prem inference
Serving multiple modalities and backends behind one API for applications and automation
Building local agents with tools, knowledge bases, skills, MCP, and terminal workflows
strengths: Supports text generation, vision, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, image/video generation, embeddings, reranking, and realtime APIs
OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible interfaces minimize client-side rewrites
Model Gallery, CLI, YAML configuration, and `/models/apply` simplify installing and managing models
Built-in LocalAGI agents run in-process with tools, memory, RAG collections, skills, SSE streaming, and import/export
gettingStarted: Run LocalAI with the official container image, mapping a persistent models directory and port 8080.
Install a model from the gallery or apply a model configuration, then verify it with `GET /v1/models`.
Send a test request to `/v1/chat/completions` or another modality endpoint using the installed model name.
Set authentication and network restrictions before exposing the server, then enable agents/MCP only for trusted workflows.
usageNotes: LocalAI is free and open source; hardware, model licenses, and optional external providers have separate terms or costs.
Feature availability depends on the selected backend and model; inspect `/.well-known/localai.json` and the compatibility docs instead of assuming every endpoint works.
Protect the API with `LOCALAI_API_KEY` or configured user authentication before allowing LAN or internet access.
Agents and terminal actions can call code, web, APIs, and files; use approval gates, least-privilege mounts, and trusted skills.
Use persistent volumes for models and pin a tested container/binary version for production rather than relying only on `latest`.
priceDetails: LocalAI is free and open source to self-host. Infrastructure, GPU capacity, model licenses, and any external API provider used by an agent are separate costs.
install: Recommended quick start: `docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 localai/localai:latest`; binaries and other OCI-compatible installation paths are documented at https://localai.io/docs/getting-started/.
start: Start the server on port 8080, install a model from the gallery, then call `http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions` with that model.

name: LibreChat
description: Open-source self-hosted conversational AI platform for many model providers, custom agents, RAG file search, web search, code execution, artifacts, and MCP tools.
bestFor: Teams that need one web interface for cloud APIs and self-hosted/local model servers
Building no-code assistants with files, tools, code interpreter, memory, and custom instructions
Organizations requiring self-hosted data control, authentication, roles, and audit-friendly configuration
strengths: Connects OpenAI-compatible providers, Ollama, and other endpoints while retaining provider-specific configuration
Agents support file handling, RAG API search, function tools, MCP servers, code execution, image generation, and web search
Conversation features include branching/forks, temporary chats, imports, share links, resumable streams, and full-text search
Self-hosted deployments support Docker, npm, Helm, MongoDB, Meilisearch, vector storage, OAuth2/SAML/LDAP, and granular permissions
gettingStarted: Clone LibreChat, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, and use the recommended Docker Compose setup.
Configure at least one provider such as OpenAI-compatible API, Ollama, or another supported endpoint, then create an account in the web UI.
Upload a document and test the RAG flow, or create an Agent with explicit instructions and only the tools it needs.
Configure authentication, secrets, MCP ACLs, and persistent storage before opening the deployment to a team.
usageNotes: LibreChat is free and open source to self-host; model/API providers, search services, storage, and infrastructure have separate costs.
Docker Compose is the recommended local installation and includes MongoDB, Meilisearch, RAG API, and vector database services.
MCP servers can be configured in `librechat.yaml` or at runtime, with user-specific connections and ACLs for sharing.
Code Interpreter and agent tools execute code or external actions; sandbox them, limit credentials, and review approvals and mounts.
The application is a self-hosted web app rather than a native desktop installer; Windows users commonly run it through Docker Desktop.
priceDetails: LibreChat is free and open source for self-hosting. Hosting infrastructure and connected model, embedding, web-search, and storage providers are billed separately.
install: Recommended Docker setup is documented at https://www.librechat.ai/docs/local/docker; manual npm and Helm installation paths are also supported.
start: Clone the repository, copy `.env.example` to `.env`, run `docker compose up -d`, then open the local LibreChat web interface.

name: BoltAI
description: Native macOS AI workspace that brings 300+ cloud and local models, keyboard-driven inline help, agents, workflows, files, and MCP tools into the apps you already use.
bestFor: Mac power users who want instant AI assistance inside any text field or application
Comparing providers and models while keeping chats, agents, projects, and files in one native client
Private local inference through Ollama or LM Studio with optional BYOK cloud services
strengths: Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Azure, Bedrock, OpenRouter, Perplexity, Groq, Ollama, and LM Studio
Global shortcuts, AI Inline, dictation, screenshot analysis, web search, prompt libraries, and reusable AI Commands speed up repetitive work
Custom agents expose instructions, context, knowledge, tools, and MCP servers with multi-agent comparison chats
Native SwiftUI/AppKit app is sandboxed and notarized; API keys can be protected in Apple Keychain and chats remain local by default
gettingStarted: Download the macOS DMG, drag BoltAI to Applications, and launch the free trial (macOS 13+; Intel and Apple Silicon supported).
Choose a provider and add your own API key, or connect Ollama/LM Studio for local models.
Use the global shortcut for a chat or select text in another app and invoke AI Inline or an AI Command.
Create agents and projects, attach files, and configure only the MCP tools needed for each workflow.
usageNotes: BoltAI is BYOK: the app license does not include model tokens; you pay connected cloud providers directly, while local Ollama/LM Studio inference has no per-token provider bill.
The current license page lists one-time Essential, Premium, and Team purchases with one year of updates/sync included; the purchased version remains usable after that year.
Local models run through Ollama or LM Studio; BoltAI’s own in-app local inference is listed as forthcoming on the official feature page.
Prompts go directly to the selected AI service provider unless you use a local model; review provider retention and data-training settings before sensitive work.
MCP servers and AI workflows can access external tools or files, so keep configurations scoped and credentials protected.
priceDetails: Official pricing currently lists Essential at $69, Premium at $97, and Team at $400 (USD, taxes may apply). These are perpetual licenses for the purchased version with one year of updates and sync; model/API usage is separate.
install: Download the latest DMG from https://boltai.com/download, open it, and drag BoltAI into Applications.
start: Launch BoltAI, add a provider/API key or connect Ollama/LM Studio, then use the menu bar or global shortcut to start chatting.

name: KoboldCpp
description: Single-file local inference server and KoboldAI interface for GGUF/GGML models, with CPU/GPU offload, roleplay/story tools, multimodal extras, and compatible APIs.
bestFor: Private local storytelling, roleplay, adventure, and long-form writing with persistent world information
Running GGUF language models on Windows, macOS, or Linux without a package-heavy installation
Developers needing Kobold, OpenAI-compatible, Ollama, or image/audio API routes around local models
strengths: A self-contained executable runs GGUF models with CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, CLBlast, or other supported acceleration paths
Bundled KoboldAI Lite UI includes memory, world info, author’s note, characters, scenarios, editing, and save formats
Provides KoboldCpp, OpenAI, Ollama, A1111/Forge, ComfyUI, Whisper transcription, XTTS, and OpenAI speech-compatible APIs
Also supports Stable Diffusion image generation, Whisper speech-to-text, OuteTTS, and vision models where configured
gettingStarted: Download the official binary for your operating system from the LostRuins/koboldcpp releases page.
Launch `koboldcpp.exe` on Windows or the platform binary, choose a GGUF model, and set context/GPU-layer options for your hardware.
Open the local web UI and select Chat, Instruct, Storywriter, or Adventure mode, then tune memory and world info as needed.
For integrations, start the server and point an OpenAI client at `http://localhost:5001/v1` or use the documented `/api` route.
usageNotes: KoboldCpp is free and open source; model files are downloaded separately and remain subject to each model’s license.
The executable is self-contained and needs no installer or external runtime, but GPU builds and drivers must match your hardware.
GGUF is the primary supported format; legacy GGML `.bin` files may work with reduced access to newer features.
Local APIs bind to the machine running the server; add your own network authentication and firewall rules before exposing them beyond localhost.
Generation quality, context capacity, and speed vary with quantization, model architecture, RAM/VRAM, and GPU offload settings.
priceDetails: KoboldCpp is free and open source. There is no hosted usage fee; model downloads, hardware, and any model-specific commercial license are separate.
install: Download the latest ready-to-use binary from https://github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest; Windows users can run the `.exe` directly without installation.
start: Run the binary, select a GGUF model, configure GPU layers if desired, and start the local server to open the bundled KoboldAI Lite UI.

name: llama.cpp
description: Portable C/C++ inference toolkit for running GGUF language and multimodal models locally, with CLI tools, quantization utilities, and an OpenAI-compatible server.
bestFor: Developers embedding efficient local inference into C/C++ or service applications
Running quantized GGUF models on CPU, Apple Silicon, NVIDIA/AMD GPU, Intel hardware, or other supported backends
Serving local text, vision, audio, embeddings, and multimodal models behind a familiar HTTP API
strengths: Includes `llama-cli` for interactive inference and `llama-server` for an OpenAI-compatible REST API
Supports direct Hugging Face model downloads with `-hf`, local GGUF files, conversion, and 1.5–8 bit quantization
Hardware backends include Metal, CUDA, HIP, Vulkan, SYCL, BLAS, WebGPU, OpenCL, and more
Multimodal support can accept image, audio, and video inputs through supported models and projectors
gettingStarted: Install a prebuilt release, Homebrew/winget/conda package, Docker image, or build llama.cpp from source.
Run a local GGUF file with `llama-cli -m my_model.gguf`, or download a compatible Hugging Face model with `-hf org/model`.
Start `llama-server -hf ggml-org/gemma-3-1b-it-GGUF` and connect an OpenAI client to its local endpoint.
Tune context, GPU offload, batching, and sampling options for the model and hardware; use a separate embedding model for RAG.
usageNotes: llama.cpp is free and open source; model weights and datasets have their own licenses and may impose commercial restrictions.
GGUF is the native model format. Other formats must be converted and often quantized before efficient local use.
The server is local by default; add network authentication, TLS, and firewall controls before exposing it outside a trusted machine.
Multimodal server support is experimental and requires compatible model/projector files; verify the model’s documented capabilities.
Inference speed and memory usage depend on quantization, context length, backend, GPU offload, and model architecture.
priceDetails: llama.cpp is free and open source with no hosted usage fee. Compute, storage, model licenses, and any third-party hosting are separate.
install: Install via Homebrew, winget, Nix, conda-forge, Docker, prebuilt releases, or a source build as documented in the official README.
start: Run `llama-cli -hf <org>/<model>` for a local chat, or launch `llama-server -hf <org>/<model>` for the HTTP API.

name: vLLM
description: High-throughput serving engine for running LLMs on your own GPUs.
bestFor: Self-hosting open-weight language models behind an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API.
High-throughput and memory-efficient serving on local or cloud GPU infrastructure.
Replacing an existing OpenAI API integration with a controllable model-serving layer.
strengths: The `vllm serve` command starts an OpenAI-compatible server, defaulting to `http://localhost:8000`.
The server exposes Completions, Responses, Chat Completions, Embeddings, Transcriptions, and Translation APIs for supported model types.
Chat Completions supports model-dependent tool calls, including optional parallel tool calls.
The server can require API keys through `--api-key` or the `VLLM_API_KEY` environment variable and can accept multiple keys for rotation.
Distributed serving is documented with tensor parallelism and Ray across multiple GPUs.
gettingStarted: Install vLLM in an environment with compatible hardware and dependencies.
Start a server with `vllm serve <model-id>`, for example `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct`.
Point an OpenAI-compatible client to `http://localhost:8000/v1` and use the served model ID.
Review the model tokenizer chat template and generation configuration; pass `--generation-config vllm` when the repository defaults should not be applied.
For multi-GPU deployment, configure tensor parallel size and the documented distributed executor backend.
usageNotes: Only one model is hosted per default server instance; run separate instances or use a routing layer for multiple models.
API compatibility is model-dependent: chat models need a chat template, embeddings need an embedding model, and ASR endpoints need an ASR model.
The local server is not protected by an API key unless `--api-key` or `VLLM_API_KEY` is configured; do not expose it publicly without access controls.
Model-generated parallel tool calls depend on the model; setting `parallel_tool_calls: true` does not guarantee multiple calls.
GPU memory, batching, quantization, and distributed settings must be sized for the selected model and workload.

name: Together AI
description: Hosted platform for running, fine-tuning, evaluating, and deploying 100+ open-source models through serverless or dedicated GPU endpoints.

Production workloads needing reserved hardware, predictable latency, autoscaling, or custom fine-tuned models
Applications using OpenAI-compatible chat, vision, image, speech, embedding, and batch APIs
strengths: Serverless and dedicated endpoints share the same inference API, making prototype-to-production migration straightforward
Supports chat/completions, vision, image generation, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, embeddings, reranking, and batch jobs
Fine-tuning and custom model upload let teams train on their data and serve adapters or weights on dedicated infrastructure
Official Python and TypeScript SDKs plus OpenAI compatibility simplify integration with existing stacks
