Choose a current model from the serverless catalog and call `https://api.together.ai/v1/chat/completions` with the SDK or OpenAI client.
Use embeddings for search/RAG, or submit batch jobs when asynchronous processing is more efficient.
For steady traffic or fine-tuned models, provision a dedicated endpoint and keep the same inference client configuration.

The OpenAI-compatible base URL is `https://api.together.ai/v1`, but OpenAI model IDs are not valid Together model names.

Fine-tuned and uploaded models may require dedicated endpoints, Hugging Face/S3 access, and additional storage or GPU costs.
Keep API keys server-side and review model licenses, training-data rights, retention, and regional processing requirements before production use.
priceDetails: Serverless inference is billed per token; dedicated endpoints are billed by GPU hardware time. Embeddings, audio, image, video, batch, fine-tuning, and storage each have current rates on https://www.together.ai/pricing.
install: No local installation is required. Install the official Python or TypeScript SDK, or use any OpenAI-compatible client pointed at `https://api.together.ai/v1`.
start: Create an API key, set `TOGETHER_API_KEY`, choose a model from the catalog, and send a chat completion request.

name: Fireworks AI
description: Inference platform for open models and custom fine-tunes with production APIs.
bestFor: Production inference with open-source models through serverless APIs.
Custom deployments, fine-tuned models, and workloads that benefit from managed GPU capacity.
Large asynchronous workloads through batch inference jobs.

Serverless models can be discovered through the SDK by filtering for `supports_serverless=true`.
The platform supports serverless inference, dedicated deployments, fine-tuning, and batch inference.
Fine-tuned models can be deployed with the `firectl deployment create` command.
Official documentation covers Python SDK access and OpenAI SDK usage, including multimodal fine-tuned models.
gettingStarted: Create a Fireworks account and API key, then store the key in a server-side secret manager.
Install the Fireworks SDK or the OpenAI SDK and configure `base_url` as `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1`.
Choose a serverless model and send a chat completion request with the model path and messages.
For a custom model, fine-tune it first and create a dedicated deployment with `firectl deployment create <FINE_TUNED_MODEL_ID>`.
For bulk processing, create a batch inference job with input and output dataset IDs.
usageNotes: An API key is required to authenticate requests and track usage; keep it out of browser code and repositories.
Check serverless model availability through the documented model listing instead of assuming every model is serverless.
Dedicated deployments and fine-tuning introduce separate resource, capacity, and billing considerations; verify current pricing before launch.
Use batch inference for asynchronous bulk workloads rather than holding many interactive requests open.
Use service accounts and organization access controls for production automation where applicable.

name: Replicate
description: Cloud platform for running, fine-tuning, publishing, and deploying machine-learning models through a versioned API, web playground, and managed hardware.
bestFor: Calling image, video, audio, speech, and language models without operating GPU infrastructure
Rapidly prototyping model ideas in a browser playground before integrating via Python, JavaScript, or HTTP
Production deployments needing custom models, dedicated hardware, autoscaling, and webhook-driven jobs
strengths: Public community models, maintained official models, and custom models share a clear prediction workflow

Official Python and JavaScript clients plus a documented HTTP API make integration language-agnostic
gettingStarted: Create a Replicate account and store `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN` only in a server-side secret.
Open a model’s playground, inspect its input schema, and run a sample prediction before writing integration code.
Use the community, official-model, or deployment prediction endpoint as appropriate; poll or request a webhook for async results.
For custom work, fine-tune a supported model or package your own code with Cog, then deploy it with the hardware and scaling settings you need.
usageNotes: Replicate is usage-based: public models are billed for actual compute time or the model’s predictable metric; dedicated deployments use reserved hardware rates.
Official models are maintained, always warm, and have stable APIs; community models can have different availability, cold starts, and pricing.
Webhooks can be retried or delivered more than once, so verify signatures, return 2xx quickly, and make handlers idempotent.
Keep API tokens out of browser code and repositories; use a backend or short-lived proxy for user-facing applications.
Model outputs, training data, and custom weights remain subject to the model author’s license and Replicate’s current retention/security terms.
priceDetails: Pricing varies by model and hardware: official models use predictable per-output metrics, while other models and deployments charge for the hardware time actually used. Check the model page and https://replicate.com/pricing before estimating cost.
install: No local installation is required. Install the official Python or JavaScript client, or send authenticated HTTPS requests to the Replicate API.
start: Choose a model at https://replicate.com/explore, run it in the playground, then create predictions with `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN`.

name: Baseten
description: Platform for deploying and scaling custom and open models as APIs.
bestFor: Deploying and serving custom AI models with managed production infrastructure.

Model caching can use private S3 storage configured through Baseten Secrets Manager.
gettingStarted: Create a Baseten account and API key, and store `BASETEN_API_KEY` in a secure server-side environment.
Install or run Truss and create a model configuration with the required accelerator and runtime settings.
Push the configuration with `uvx truss push` and record the returned model and deployment IDs.
Configure production autoscaling through the deployment API after measuring workload concurrency and latency.
Add secrets through Baseten Secrets Manager rather than placing cloud credentials in model configuration or source control.
usageNotes: Keep Baseten API keys and cloud storage credentials server-side and outside the repository.
GPU and accelerator selection directly affects cost and performance; validate the model's resource requirements before deployment.
Autoscaling settings such as minimum and maximum replicas, scale-down delay, and concurrency targets should be tuned from observed traffic.
Private S3 model caches require correctly configured secrets and runtime secret names.
Treat observability and deployment IDs as production configuration; verify the active deployment before changing autoscaling.

name: fal.ai
description: Inference API for generative image, video, and audio models.

Trying models in browser widgets or routing API calls through multiple inference providers

priceDetails: Public Hub usage is free. Inference Providers are pay-as-you-go after included credits; dedicated Inference Endpoints and upgraded Space hardware are billed by compute time, while PRO/Team/Enterprise plans include additional credits and features.
install: Install the current Hub CLI with the official installer or Python package, then use `hf auth login`; SDKs include `huggingface_hub` and `huggingface.js`.
start: Open https://huggingface.co/models, choose a model or Space, then use its widget, `hf` CLI, InferenceClient, or deployment guide.

name: DeepInfra
description: Hosted inference API for open text, image, and audio models.

Migrating OpenAI-compatible applications to pay-per-token inference without managing GPUs.

Priority inference carries a premium over standard usage; verify current pricing before selecting it broadly.

Model IDs and availability change; use the current catalog rather than hard-coding unsupported models.

name: Nebius AI Studio

name: Novita AI

name: Cloudflare Workers AI
description: Serverless inference for open models on Cloudflare’s global network through Workers AI bindings, REST API, and AI Gateway.
bestFor: Low-latency inference inside Cloudflare Workers and Pages
Adding text, image, speech, embedding, and reranking models without GPU operations
Building AI apps with edge deployment, observability, caching, and provider controls
strengths: AI binding exposes models directly as env.AI in a Worker
Catalog includes hosted text, image, audio, embedding, and multimodal models
REST API allows inference from apps outside Workers
AI Gateway adds centralized logging, caching, rate limits, retries, and fallbacks
Global edge deployment keeps request handling close to users
gettingStarted: Create a Cloudflare account and Workers project, then install Wrangler.
Add an AI binding named AI in wrangler.toml or the dashboard.
Choose an exact model ID from the live Workers AI catalog and call env.AI.run(model, inputs).
Deploy with npx wrangler deploy and test the Worker endpoint.
Use REST API or AI Gateway when calling from non-Worker services or when centralized controls are needed.
usageNotes: Usage-based pricing depends on model and inference units; verify current limits and rates in the pricing docs.
API tokens/account authentication are required for REST and Wrangler workflows; keep tokens out of client code.
Model IDs, capabilities, context limits, and availability change; query the current catalog before hard-coding.
Workers AI runs on Cloudflare infrastructure; review data processing, retention, model licenses, and regional needs.
Add application authentication to public Worker endpoints and apply rate limits before production traffic.
priceDetails: Usage-based Workers AI inference units with account plan allowances; check https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/ for current rates.
install: npm install -D wrangler
start: Create a Worker, add an AI binding named AI, call env.AI.run with a catalog model, then run npx wrangler deploy.
commands: npm install -D wrangler
npx wrangler login
npx wrangler deploy

name: IBM watsonx
description: Enterprise AI platform combining watsonx.ai model development and inference, watsonx.governance controls, and watsonx.data for governed data access.
bestFor: Prompting, fine-tuning, evaluating, and deploying foundation models in an enterprise workspace
Building governed RAG, agent, and generative AI applications
Teams needing IBM Granite and third-party models with IAM, auditability, and lifecycle controls
strengths: Prompt Lab provides visual experimentation with reusable prompts and model comparisons
REST API and Python SDK support inference, embeddings, tuning, deployments, and model catalog discovery
watsonx.governance adds risk, compliance, factsheets, monitoring, and policy workflows
Supports IBM and third-party foundation models, with on-demand deployment options in IBM Cloud regions
Integrated data and deployment assets help move experiments into managed production services
gettingStarted: Create an IBM Cloud account and a watsonx.ai project, then create an API key and project/space identifier.
Open Prompt Lab to compare a foundation model, parameters, templates, and sample prompts.
For code, install ibm-watsonx-ai, authenticate with IBM Cloud IAM, and construct a ModelInference client.
Deploy the prompt or model as an AI service and call its REST endpoint from your application.
Add governance checks, data connections, evaluation datasets, and monitoring before production rollout.
usageNotes: Pricing varies by trial, Essentials, Standard, model, tokens, embeddings, deployments, and region; verify the current IBM pricing page.
IBM Cloud API keys and IAM tokens are required for programmatic access; use service IDs and least-privilege roles.
Model availability and deployment methods vary by region and cloud type; check the current supported-model matrix.
Prompt Lab and API requests may use project-scoped assets; confirm access, retention, and data residency for sensitive inputs.
Review model licenses, guardrails, evaluation results, and governance policies before using outputs in consequential workflows.
priceDetails: Trial and paid Essentials/Standard plans with model and service usage pricing; see https://www.ibm.com/products/watsonx-ai/pricing for current rates.
install: pip install ibm-watsonx-ai
start: Create an IBM Cloud project, open Prompt Lab, choose a foundation model, then use the generated REST or Python code for integration.
commands: pip install ibm-watsonx-ai
ibmcloud login
curl -X POST https://us-south.ml.cloud.ibm.com/ml/v1/text/generation?version=2024-05-01

name: Pinecone
description: Managed vector database for similarity search and retrieval workloads.
bestFor: Production semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, and recommendation systems.
Teams that want a managed vector database instead of operating their own indexing cluster.
Applications that need namespaces, metadata filtering, serverless indexes, or integrated embedding workflows.
strengths: Official SDKs can create serverless indexes, upsert vectors with metadata, and query top-k matches.
Namespaces isolate datasets or tenants inside an index and are created implicitly when vectors are upserted.
The platform supports custom vectors as well as integrated indexes that generate embeddings for mapped text fields.
Metadata schemas can restrict which fields are filterable to improve indexing efficiency.
Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, and Java SDKs are documented for index and vector operations.
gettingStarted: Create a Pinecone project and API key, then store `PINECONE_API_KEY` in a server-side secret.
Create a serverless index with the embedding dimension, similarity metric, cloud, and region that match your model.
Generate embeddings, upsert records with stable IDs and metadata into a namespace, and query with `topK`.
Start with a small representative dataset, validate retrieval quality, then add metadata filters and production monitoring.
usageNotes: The vector dimension must match the embedding model and index configuration; a mismatch causes failed upserts or poor retrieval.
Keep namespaces and metadata fields intentional: they affect tenant isolation, filtering behavior, and index design.
Never expose `PINECONE_API_KEY` in browser code, source control, logs, or client-downloadable configuration.
Choose cloud and region deliberately for latency, data residency, and current pricing; do not hard-code costs in the card.
Use retries only for transient failures and make ingestion jobs idempotent by using stable record IDs.

name: Weaviate
description: Open-source vector database with hybrid search and a managed cloud option.
bestFor: Cloud-native vector search and RAG applications that combine objects, embeddings, and metadata.
Teams that want managed Weaviate Cloud or a locally hosted Docker deployment.
Search experiences that need semantic, keyword, hybrid, or generative retrieval.
strengths: Collections store data objects and vectors with configurable vectorizers and index settings.
Hybrid search combines keyword and vector relevance and supports filters and result limits.
The TypeScript and Python clients support Weaviate Cloud, local instances, and custom hosts.
Indexes can use HNSW, flat, or dynamic configurations, distance metrics, quantization, and inverted indexes.
Official quickstarts cover semantic search and RAG from both Weaviate Cloud and local Docker.
gettingStarted: Choose Weaviate Cloud or run a local Docker instance for development.
Connect with the official client and keep the instance API key and provider keys in server-side secrets.
Create a collection with properties, vectorizer, distance/index configuration, and any generative integration.
Import representative objects, run semantic and hybrid searches, then add filters and RAG only after retrieval quality is measured.
usageNotes: The vectorizer and model determine embedding dimensions and behavior; keep collection configuration aligned with the model.
Provider headers such as `X-OpenAI-Api-Key` or `X-Cohere-Api-Key` are separate from the Weaviate instance API key.
Never expose Weaviate or inference keys in browser code, public repositories, or client-downloadable configuration.
Local development examples may use unauthenticated localhost; configure API-key authentication and HTTPS for shared or production instances.
Choose HNSW, flat, dynamic indexing, quantization, and inverted-index fields based on dataset size, filtering needs, latency, and recall.

name: Qdrant
description: Open-source vector search engine with filtering and a managed cloud service.
bestFor: Self-hosted or managed vector search for semantic retrieval and RAG applications.
Teams that need payload filtering, collection-level control, and REST/gRPC access.
Local development that can later move to a production Qdrant deployment.
strengths: Stores points with vectors and payload metadata, then searches them by similarity.
Collections define vector size and distance metric; payload indexes support efficient filtering.
The Search API can restrict results to points matching a filter and returns ranked IDs by default.
Official clients cover Python, TypeScript, Rust, Java, Go, and C# alongside REST and gRPC.
Docker deployments can persist data in a mounted storage directory.
gettingStarted: Run Qdrant locally with Docker or create a managed cluster, then configure the endpoint and API key.
Create a collection with the embedding dimension and distance metric used by your model.
Upsert points with stable IDs, vectors, and payload metadata into the collection.
Query the collection with a vector and optional payload filter, then inspect retrieval quality on representative data.
usageNotes: Vector size must match the embedding model; changing models usually requires a new collection or a migration plan.
Create payload indexes for fields used frequently in filters, and keep payload schemas intentional for performance.
Secure deployed instances with an API key and HTTPS; never expose admin credentials in frontend code or source control.
Mount persistent storage for Docker so data survives container recreation and upgrades.
Design stable point IDs and idempotent upserts so ingestion can be safely retried after transient failures.

name: Milvus
description: Open-source distributed vector database for large-scale similarity search.
bestFor: High-scale vector search and retrieval for AI applications with large unstructured datasets.
Teams choosing between Milvus Lite, self-hosted Docker/Kubernetes, and managed Zilliz Cloud.
Search systems that need vector similarity, scalar filters, hybrid ranking, or full-text capabilities.
strengths: Collections define schemas, vector dimensions, metadata fields, indexes, and consistency behavior.
MilvusClient supports insert, vector search, filtered query, and delete operations.
Milvus Lite can use a local database file, while server and Zilliz Cloud use network URIs and tokens.
AutoIndex, COSINE distance, payload filters, and hybrid rankers cover common RAG retrieval designs.
Official SDKs include PyMilvus and Node.js, with additional clients and integrations.
gettingStarted: Choose Milvus Lite for a local prototype, Docker/Kubernetes for self-hosting, or Zilliz Cloud for managed infrastructure.
Create a collection schema with a primary key, vector field dimension, text/metadata fields, and an index.
Insert stable records and load the collection when using a server deployment.
Search with a query vector, limit, output fields, and an optional filter; measure recall before tuning indexes.
usageNotes: The embedding dimension must match the collection vector field and model output.
Use API tokens for Zilliz Cloud and protect them as server-side secrets; do not expose credentials in frontend code.
A local file URI is convenient for experiments but is not a substitute for backups, access control, or a multi-user deployment.
Choose consistency, index type, metric, and hybrid ranker based on latency, recall, update frequency, and dataset size.
Make ingestion idempotent and validate filter expressions so retries do not duplicate or delete unintended records.

name: Chroma
description: Open-source embedding database for building retrieval features in applications.
bestFor: Fast local prototyping of embedding search, RAG, and memory features for LLM applications.
Python and JavaScript projects that want a simple embedding database API.
Workloads that may start with local persistence and later move to a managed Chroma Cloud deployment.
strengths: Collections store documents, embeddings, metadata, and stable IDs with add, get, and query operations.
PersistentClient automatically saves local database state to a configured filesystem path.
Built-in and provider-specific embedding functions can be attached to collections for consistent cross-client behavior.
Metadata filters support operators such as `$in` for narrowing retrieval and document reads.
The same application pattern can target local Chroma or Chroma Cloud with an API key.
gettingStarted: Install the Python or JavaScript client and choose an in-memory, persistent local, server, or cloud deployment.
Create or retrieve a collection with an explicit embedding function and distance configuration.
Add documents with unique IDs and useful metadata, then query by text or embeddings.
Evaluate retrieval on representative queries, add metadata filters, and configure persistence before sharing the application.
usageNotes: Persisted local data is stored at the path passed to `PersistentClient`; back up that directory if it contains valuable data.
Keep the embedding function and model configuration consistent when multiple clients read the same collection.
Use unique stable IDs and idempotent ingestion so re-running an import does not create duplicate records.
Protect `CHROMA_API_KEY` and other provider keys in server-side secrets; never expose them in browser code or source control.
Local embedded mode is convenient for development, while multi-user or high-availability needs should be evaluated against server/cloud deployment requirements.

name: LangSmith
description: Tracing, evaluation, and monitoring tools for LLM applications.
bestFor: Tracing, debugging, evaluating, and monitoring LLM applications in development and production.
Teams that need datasets, evaluators, feedback loops, and regression checks for AI quality.
LangChain and other AI applications that need a centralized observability workspace.
strengths: Tracing records application runs so prompts, outputs, latency, and failures can be inspected.
Datasets and evaluators support repeatable offline testing and quality comparisons.
Online evaluation can monitor production traces for safety and quality and feed failing examples back into datasets.
Projects organize traces and let teams separate environments or experiments.
SDKs and environment variables make tracing practical across local apps and deployed services.
gettingStarted: Create a LangSmith account and API key, then store `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` in server-side secrets.
Set `LANGSMITH_TRACING=true`, `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT=https://api.smith.langchain.com`, and a project name.
Run a small representative application flow and inspect its trace in the LangSmith workspace.
Create a dataset from representative and failing examples, add evaluators, and compare changes before shipping.
usageNotes: Never expose `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` or model-provider keys in browser bundles, repositories, prompts, or logs.
Tracing can contain prompts, outputs, metadata, and user data; define retention, redaction, and access controls before enabling production capture.
Use separate projects for development, staging, and production so experiments do not pollute operational metrics.
Online evaluation adds processing and cost; choose evaluators that measure the quality and safety risks relevant to your application.
Background callbacks can affect latency and trace completeness; configure them according to the deployment environment.

name: Langfuse
description: Open-source LLM engineering platform for tracing, prompt management, evaluations, datasets, metrics, and production analytics.
bestFor: Tracing LLM calls, agents, RAG chains, costs, latency, and errors
Versioning prompts and linking prompt revisions to observed generations
Running datasets, experiments, LLM-as-a-judge, and regression evaluations in cloud or self-hosted deployments
strengths: Python and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs send traces asynchronously with OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation
Prompt Management versions prompts and supports cached retrieval without adding request latency
Datasets, experiments, scores, and evaluators connect offline testing with production traces
Cloud and self-hosted options support API access, dashboards, and data export
Integrations cover OpenAI, LangChain, Vercel AI SDK, and many agent frameworks
gettingStarted: Create a Langfuse Cloud project or deploy the open-source stack with Docker/Kubernetes.
Create project public and secret keys and store them as LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY and LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY.
Install the Python or JavaScript SDK, instrument an LLM call, and flush traces before process exit.
Create a versioned prompt in Prompt Management and fetch it by name from your application.
Add a dataset and evaluation experiment, then inspect traces, scores, token usage, and latency in the UI.
usageNotes: Cloud pricing and limits vary by plan and event volume; self-hosting has infrastructure and operations costs. Check https://langfuse.com/pricing.
API keys are required for Cloud and SDK ingestion; keep them server-side and scope projects appropriately.
Tracing captures prompts, inputs, outputs, and metadata by default; configure masking and sampling before sending sensitive data.
Prompt versions are cached and fetched by label; deploy safely by pinning labels or versions and monitoring linked traces.
Review model-provider terms, retention, access controls, and regional compliance for observability data.
priceDetails: Freemium Cloud plan with usage limits plus paid tiers; core platform is open source and self-hostable. See https://langfuse.com/pricing and https://langfuse.com/pricing-self-host.
install: npm install langfuse or pip install langfuse
start: Create a project at https://cloud.langfuse.com, copy API keys, install an SDK, and wrap your first LLM call with Langfuse tracing.
commands: npm install langfuse
pip install langfuse
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up

name: Arize Phoenix
description: Open-source AI observability and evaluation platform for tracing LLM, agent, and RAG applications with OpenTelemetry and OpenInference.
bestFor: Visualizing traces, latency, token usage, retrieval, and errors in LLM apps
Evaluating responses with datasets, experiments, annotations, and LLM-as-a-judge metrics
Prompt engineering and debugging in a local or hosted Phoenix workspace
strengths: Phoenix-aware OpenTelemetry helpers instrument popular LLM and framework integrations
Prompt Playground supports prompt/model iteration while linking results to traces and experiments
Phoenix Evals provides reusable evaluators and custom scoring workflows
Projects organize traces and allow datasets to be exported for regression testing
Runs locally with no account by default, or connects to Phoenix Cloud with API authentication
gettingStarted: For local development, install Phoenix and run phoenix serve, then open the local UI.
For Phoenix Cloud, create a free space and set PHOENIX_API_KEY and PHOENIX_COLLECTOR_ENDPOINT.
Install arize-phoenix-otel plus the integration package for your model provider.
Register a tracer, set a project name, and instrument one representative LLM or RAG request.
Create a dataset or evaluate traces with arize-phoenix-evals, then inspect scores and regressions in the UI.
usageNotes: The open-source local workflow does not require an account; Phoenix Cloud requires a space and API key.
Cloud and hosted limits, retention, and pricing can change; verify the current Arize Phoenix plan before production use.
Traces may contain prompts, retrieved documents, outputs, and metadata; configure masking, sampling, and access controls for sensitive data.
Phoenix is distinct from Arize AX and uses different endpoints and APIs; select the product explicitly.
Review evaluator bias, model-provider terms, and human review requirements before acting on automated scores.
priceDetails: Open-source and self-hostable; Phoenix Cloud offers a free space and paid limits/features. Check https://arize.com/pricing for current hosted terms.
install: pip install arize-phoenix arize-phoenix-otel arize-phoenix-evals
start: Run phoenix serve locally or create a Phoenix Cloud space, configure the collector endpoint, then instrument your first LLM call.
commands: pip install arize-phoenix-otel arize-phoenix-client arize-phoenix-evals
phoenix serve
npm install @arizeai/phoenix-otel

name: Braintrust
description: AI quality platform for prompt iteration, datasets, experiments, production tracing, and automated evaluation.
bestFor: Measuring LLM and agent quality with repeatable datasets and scorers
Comparing prompt/model versions in a playground before deployment
Tracing production applications and running online evaluations to catch regressions
strengths: Evaluations combine versioned data, arbitrary task functions, and custom or LLM-as-a-judge scores
Playgrounds let teams test prompts against datasets and compare versions side by side
Experiments are immutable, shareable snapshots suitable for CI/CD regression gates
Production traces expose nested agent/tool/LLM spans, latency, tokens, and errors
SDKs and API support TypeScript, Python, Go, Ruby, Java, and OpenAI integrations
gettingStarted: Create a free Braintrust workspace and project, then generate an API key.
Install the Braintrust SDK for your language and set BRAINTRUST_API_KEY.
Create a dataset with inputs and expected outputs, define a task, and add scoring functions.
Run an Eval locally or in CI to create a permanent experiment and inspect the results in the UI.
Add tracing and online scoring to production logs, then promote successful prompt versions.
usageNotes: Cloud usage and retention limits vary by plan; confirm current pricing and data terms before production use.
API keys are required for SDK, CLI, and API calls; store them in secret managers and scope project access.
Datasets and traces can contain user prompts and outputs; redact sensitive data and configure privacy controls.
Experiments are immutable snapshots while playground runs are for iteration; use experiments for release gates.
Automated scores are signals, not truth; combine deterministic checks with human review for consequential decisions.
priceDetails: Freemium hosted platform with plan-based usage, retention, and evaluation limits. Check https://www.braintrust.dev/pricing for current terms.
install: npm install braintrust or pip install braintrust
start: Sign up at https://www.braintrust.dev, create a project and API key, then run the evaluation quickstart with a dataset, task, and scorer.
commands: npm install braintrust
pip install braintrust
npx braintrust eval

name: AgentOps
description: AI agent observability SDK and dashboard for tracing sessions, LLM calls, tool usage, costs, errors, and agent workflows.
bestFor: Monitoring and debugging multi-step AI agents in development and production
Tracking LLM cost, latency, tokens, errors, and session replay
Instrumenting OpenAI, CrewAI, LangChain, AutoGen, Anthropic, Ollama, and custom tools
strengths: Python and TypeScript SDKs provide automatic instrumentation with a small initialization step
Hierarchical sessions, agents, operations, traces, and tools show complete workflow context
Dashboard surfaces token usage, model costs, latency, errors, and replayable agent sessions
Decorators allow precise tracing of custom operations, tools, and agent boundaries
Open-source SDK and broad framework integrations reduce vendor-specific instrumentation work
gettingStarted: Create an AgentOps account and copy an API key from the dashboard, or run the local/open-source app if self-hosting.
Install the SDK with pip install agentops or npm install agentops and set AGENTOPS_API_KEY.
Call agentops.init() before your agent framework or LLM client starts.
Use session, agent, operation, tool, or trace decorators for custom workflow boundaries.
Run the agent, open the dashboard session, and review traces, costs, errors, and token metrics.
usageNotes: A hosted account and API key are required to send telemetry to the AgentOps dashboard; local/open-source usage may differ.
Tracing can capture prompts, tool inputs, outputs, and metadata; redact secrets and private user data before export.
Supported integrations, model-cost tables, quotas, and retention policies can change; verify current docs.
Use auto_start_session=False when you need explicit lifecycle control for background jobs or nested workflows.
Observability data is diagnostic, not a quality guarantee; combine traces with evals and human review for critical agents.
priceDetails: Hosted pricing and free limits vary by workspace and event volume; check https://agentops.ai/pricing for current terms. The SDK is open source.
install: pip install agentops python-dotenv
start: Set AGENTOPS_API_KEY, call agentops.init() before your agent code, run a supported workflow, and inspect the resulting session in the dashboard.
commands: pip install agentops python-dotenv
npm install agentops
python your_agent.py

name: Portkey
description: AI gateway and control plane with a universal API, provider routing, fallbacks, caching, guardrails, budgets, and observability.
bestFor: Routing one application across many LLM providers and model families
Adding reliability, cost controls, caching, retries, and failover without rewriting application code
Centralizing logs, governance, guardrails, and access to production model traffic
strengths: OpenAI-compatible REST and SDK interfaces support hundreds of models and providers
Gateway configs enable fallbacks, conditional routing, load balancing, retries, circuit breakers, canary tests, and timeouts
Simple and semantic caching can reduce repeated latency and spend
Guardrails, rate limits, token budgets, and provider virtual keys centralize policy
Open-source gateway can run locally with npx @portkey-ai/gateway or be connected to the hosted control plane
gettingStarted: Create a Portkey account and API key, then add provider credentials as virtual keys or secure integrations.
Install the Portkey SDK or reuse the OpenAI SDK with PORTKEY_GATEWAY_URL as base URL.
Create a gateway config for a primary model, fallback chain, cache, timeout, and retry policy.
Send a representative chat, Responses API, embedding, image, or multimodal request through the gateway.
Inspect logs and costs, then add guardrails, rate limits, and canary routing before production traffic.
usageNotes: Hosted pricing and free limits vary by workspace, requests, and enterprise features; check https://portkey.ai/pricing.
API keys and provider credentials are required for hosted use; keep both server-side and rotate them regularly.
Gateway configs can alter routing and provider data residency; review fallbacks, regions, retention, and model terms.
Caching may return earlier outputs and semantic matches; avoid caching requests containing secrets or highly personal data.
Guardrails and automated retries improve resilience but do not replace output validation, safety testing, or human review.
priceDetails: Hosted freemium and paid plans with usage/feature limits; the open-source gateway is available for self-hosting. Check https://portkey.ai/pricing.
install: pip install -U portkey-ai openai
start: Create a Portkey workspace and provider key, install the SDK, set the gateway base URL, and send an OpenAI-compatible request.
commands: pip install -U portkey-ai openai
npm install portkey-ai openai
npx @portkey-ai/gateway

name: Galileo
description: Generative AI observability, evaluation, and guardrails platform for tracing LLM applications and agent workflows.
bestFor: Monitoring production LLM quality, latency, costs, and failures
Evaluating RAG and conversational outputs with built-in and custom metrics
Adding runtime guardrails and protected stages to AI applications
strengths: SDKs and OpenAI wrappers capture traces, sessions, projects, and log streams
Built-in scorers help measure hallucination, relevance, toxicity, and other generative quality signals
Experiments and datasets support repeatable evaluation and model/prompt comparisons
Protect stages and rulesets can enforce guardrails before or during generation
Python and TypeScript APIs support direct logging and framework integrations
gettingStarted: Create a Galileo project and log stream, then copy the API key from the console.
Install the Python or TypeScript SDK and set GALILEO_API_KEY, GALILEO_PROJECT, and GALILEO_LOG_STREAM.
Wrap or instrument an OpenAI/LLM call, run a representative request, and inspect the trace in Galileo.
Create an evaluation dataset and configure built-in or custom scorers for your use case.
Add guardrail stages, sampling, and human feedback before exposing the workflow to production users.
usageNotes: A hosted Galileo account and API key are required for normal cloud logging; confirm current plan and retention terms.
Traces may include prompts, retrieved documents, outputs, and metadata; redact sensitive data and review access controls.
Metric definitions and model/provider support can change; validate scorers on representative examples before gating releases.
Guardrails can block or modify requests and introduce latency; test false positives and failure behavior.
Keep provider API keys separate from Galileo credentials and use environment variables or secret managers.
priceDetails: Paid hosted platform with plan-dependent usage and features; check https://galileo.ai/pricing for current terms.
install: pip install "galileo[openai]" python-dotenv
start: Create a Galileo project and log stream, set the required environment variables, install the SDK, and send one instrumented LLM request.
commands: pip install "galileo[openai]" python-dotenv
npm install galileo

name: Weights & Biases Weave
description: W&B Weave toolkit for tracing, evaluating, versioning, and monitoring generative AI applications.
bestFor: Tracing LLM inputs, outputs, tool calls, and nested agent workflows
Building versioned datasets, models, scorers, and repeatable evaluations
Monitoring production quality and collecting feedback in the W&B UI
strengths: Python and TypeScript SDKs provide automatic integrations plus custom @weave.op tracing
Models, prompts, datasets, and scorers are versioned for apples-to-apples comparisons
Evaluation workflows combine test cases, task functions, and built-in or custom scoring functions
Production traces and feedback can feed new datasets and regression tests
W&B project dashboards connect Weave quality data with broader experiment tracking
gettingStarted: Create a W&B account and API key, then install weave for Python or TypeScript.
Initialize a project with weave.init("team/project") and keep the key in an environment variable.
Instrument an LLM call or custom function with weave.op and inspect the trace in the Weave UI.
Define a versioned dataset, Model, and scorer, then run an Evaluation to compare outputs.
Add production feedback, monitors, and guardrails after validating metrics on representative cases.
usageNotes: A W&B account and API key are required for hosted tracing; verify current limits and retention for your plan.
Traces can contain prompts, outputs, retrieved documents, and metadata; redact sensitive data and configure access controls.
Python and TypeScript feature parity is not complete; check the current SDK docs before choosing advanced Model or Scorer APIs.
Evaluation scores are diagnostic signals and can encode judge bias; combine custom checks with human review.
Pin prompt/model versions and dataset revisions in release workflows so results remain reproducible.
priceDetails: Free tier available with plan-dependent hosted usage, retention, and collaboration limits; check https://wandb.ai/site/pricing.
install: pip install weave or npm install weave
start: Create a W&B project and API key, install Weave, call weave.init, then decorate one LLM or application function with weave.op.
commands: pip install weave openai
npm install weave openai
wandb login

name: Unstructured
description: Tools and APIs for turning complex documents into structured data for RAG pipelines.
bestFor: Parsing PDFs, office files, images, and other unstructured sources for RAG and agent pipelines.
Teams that need configurable partitioning, chunking, embedding, and destination connectors.
Batch ingestion from local files or cloud storage with reproducible processing stages.
strengths: Partitioning converts source files into structured elements with metadata suitable for downstream retrieval.
The Ingest CLI and Python pipeline can compose indexing, downloading, partitioning, chunking, embedding, and uploading.
Chunking strategies such as `by_title` and configurable character limits make retrieval units explicit.
Pipelines can target local directories, SQLite, Astra DB, and other documented destinations.
API-based partitioning supports high-resolution strategies and configurable PDF splitting.
gettingStarted: Choose the open-source library/CLI for local processing or the Unstructured API/Platform for managed partitioning.
Set `UNSTRUCTURED_API_KEY` and endpoint secrets server-side when using API partitioning.
Run a small sample through partitioning, inspect element metadata, then choose a chunking strategy.
Add embeddings and a destination connector only after the extracted structure and chunk boundaries look correct.
usageNotes: Partitioning, chunking, and embedding are separate stages; tune and measure each stage instead of treating ingestion as a black box.
Use environment variables for API keys, database tokens, input paths, and output paths; never commit secrets.
For PDFs, verify page splitting and failure behavior on scanned, malformed, and multi-column documents.
Restrict metadata fields deliberately so downstream database schemas do not receive unexpected columns.
Choose local processing, API, or Platform based on data residency, throughput, supported file types, and current pricing.

name: LlamaParse
description: Document parsing service from LlamaIndex for complex PDFs and tables.
bestFor: Parsing complex PDFs and documents into Markdown or structured data for RAG and agent workflows.
Document ingestion teams that need OCR, layout-aware parsing, extraction, and classification in one cloud API.
Batch processing many files with asynchronous jobs and per-job parsing tiers.
strengths: The Llama Cloud client can upload a file, create a parsing job, poll its status, and retrieve Markdown output.
Parsing can start from an uploaded file ID or a public source URL.
Batch workflows can mix parsing and schema-driven extraction jobs and report per-job results.
Agentic and cost-effective tiers let teams trade richer processing against throughput and spend.
Official Python SDK supports synchronous and asynchronous clients.
gettingStarted: Create a Llama Cloud account and store `LLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` or `LLAMA_PARSE_API_KEY` in a server-side secret.
Upload a representative PDF with purpose `parse`, then create a parsing job with the selected tier and version.
Poll `PENDING`/`RUNNING` jobs and retrieve the result with Markdown expansion when complete.
For multiple documents, use batches and validate extracted fields against a schema before indexing them.
